data.title: Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared Features, Pricing and Costs
data.ai_summary: Eight salon scheduling platforms are compared, covering Bookeo, Mangomint, Boulevard, GlossGenius, Fresha, Vagaro, Square Appointments, and Acuity Scheduling. Pricing models vary from flat tiers to per-user fees and marketplace commissions, with tradeoffs noted for each. The comparison highlights how cost structures differ across platforms.

industries.name: Personal Care & Wellness Booking Platforms (Beauty, Fitness, Spa)

data.full_text:
Home Press Release Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared: Features, Pricing And Key Differences

Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared: Features, Pricing and Key Differences Published: 29 Sep 2026 Author: Precedence Research Share: Top Scheduling Software Compared: Head-to-Head Feature Breakdown If you run a salon or a day spa and you are shopping for scheduling software right now, the hard part is not finding options. There are dozens, and most of them will take a booking, send a reminder, and hold a card. The hard part is that the platforms are priced on completely different logic, so two systems that look almost identical on a feature grid can be several thousand dollars apart over a year, depending on how many chairs you have and where your new clients come from. This is a large and growing trade, which is part of why the software market around it is so crowded. Federal labor projections have employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists growing 7 percent between 2025 and 2035, off a base of roughly 670,800 jobs. We compared eight platforms that salon and spa owners actually shortlist, and we have written every entry to the same template so the comparison is like-for-like. How This Comparison Was Put Together We started from the pages that currently rank for salon and spa scheduling queries and pulled out every vendor that appeared on more than one of them, then removed the tools that are general-purpose calendar apps with a beauty landing page attached. What was left is the eight platforms below. For each one we did the same three things. We opened the vendor's own pricing page and recorded the published numbers, including per-user charges, per-location charges and card processing rates, because those are the figures that move the annual total. We recorded the current Capterra rating and the review count, as plain text, so you can see how much evidence sits behind each score. Then we identified one limitation for every platform, including the one we placed first. We did not accept "contact us for pricing" as an answer, and no vendor paid for placement or for a particular position in the list. Ratings and prices were checked in September 2026 and they do change, so treat them as a starting point rather than a quote. The Eight Platforms At A Glance Platform Starting price Pricing model Best for Main tradeoff Capterra rating Bookeo $14.95 a month Flat tiers by staff count and booking volume Salons and spas that want a predictable bill Branches run as separate accounts 4.3 (103 reviews) Mangomint $130 a month Base fee plus per user Salons with a front desk and a full service menu High cost floor for very small teams 5.0 (344 reviews) Boulevard $140 a month per location Tiered per location Multi-location salons, spas and medspas Priced per location, entry tier caps professionals 4.6 (389 reviews) GlossGenius $24 a month Flat tiers, payments included Solo stylists and small teams Rooms, waivers and waitlist sit on higher tiers 4.8 (349 reviews) Fresha $19.95 a month Subscription plus new-client commission Salons that want marketplace demand 20 percent commission on new marketplace clients 4.8 (1,447 reviews) Vagaro $30 a month Scales with bookable calendars Mixed beauty and wellness businesses Marketing tools and branded app excluded from trial 4.7 (3,651 reviews) Square Appointments $0 a month Free tier, then per location Salons already on Square hardware No-show fees and waitlist require a paid plan 4.5 (260 reviews) Acuity Scheduling $16 a month Tiered by number of calendars Single-service providers and small studios A scheduler rather than a salon system 4.8 (5,758 reviews) 1. Bookeo Best for: salons and spas that want a predictable flat monthly bill and industry-specific scheduling rather than a percentage of every booking. If you are comparing these eight platforms on cost, this is the one where the pricing structure is the main argument. Bookeo prices on staff count and on monthly booking volume, so the bill does not move when you have a good month, and the software vendor does not take a commission out of a booking; card processing runs through Stripe, Square, or PayPal at those providers' own published rates. The appointments product is also one of three separate products (the other two are built for classes and for tours and activities), which is a different design decision from the single general-purpose system that most of this category ships. Key features Real-time booking through a widget embedded in your existing site, or a standalone branded booking page if you do not have one

Staff assigned to specific services with working hours set per staff member and per location, plus calendar sync with Google Calendar, iCal, Outlook and Office 365

Deposits, full prepayment or a card held on file, with automatic email and text reminders and online rescheduling

Client database with intake forms, prepaid packages, memberships and gift vouchers, and digital waivers as a paid add-on Pricing: five tiers, quoted on the US pricing page as Solo at $14.95, Small at $29.95, Standard at $39.95, Large at $79.95, and X-Large at $119.95 a month. The tiers run from 1 consultant and 200 bookings a month up to 60 consultants and 3,000 bookings a month. Digital waivers are an add-on at $9 to $249 a month depending on volume, and text credits are $0.09 each. The free trial is 30 days with no credit card required. Rating: 4.3 on Capterra from 103 reviews. Where it falls short: multi-branch businesses are handled through a portal in which customers search for a branch or centre and then book with that individual branch, and each branch is a standalone account that controls its own schedule, staff, customer database, sales reports and statistics. Data is not shared between branches. Each branch has its own customers, its own members and its own gift vouchers, so a voucher bought at one branch can only be redeemed at that branch. The portal manager can go into each sub-account's backend and pull portal reports (booking summaries and a revenue summary) for each sub-account, but if you are expecting one combined customer list across five sites, that is not the model. The review base is also small next to the platforms further down this list, which is worth knowing when you are reading scores. 2. Mangomint Best for: salons and spas with a front desk and a full-service menu that want one system running the floor rather than a calendar and a till kept separately. Mangomint is built on the assumption that you have a front desk and somebody standing at it. Pricing is $120 a month as a base fee plus $10 per user, so the smallest realistic monthly bill is $130, and the bill rises with headcount rather than with bookings. What you get for that is a system intended to run the whole floor rather than only the calendar, which includes point of sale, retail and inventory, forms and charting, and staff management. Key features Calendar, online booking, Express Booking and a virtual waiting room for walk-ins and gaps

Point of sale with retail and inventory, gift cards, memberships and packages

Forms and charting, client management and web chat

Staff management, reporting and multi-location support in the base plan Pricing: $120 a month base plus $10 per user, with additional locations at $120 a month each. Add-ons are priced separately, including phone at $70 a month per line, marketing from $30 a month, and payroll at $50 a month plus $8 per worker. Card processing is 2.45 percent plus 15 cents in person and 2.90 percent plus 30 cents for virtual transactions. A free trial account is available. Rating: 5.0 on Capterra from 344 reviews. Where it falls short: the cost floor. A three-stylist salon is at $150 a month before a single add-on, and a solo operator is paying for a front-desk system that will not be used. The reporting and inventory depth is real, but it is depth you have to be big enough to need. 3. Boulevard Best for: multi-location salons, spas and medspas that need per-location control, per-location reporting and treatment-side depth. Boulevard is priced and reported per location, and that is the design assumption underneath the whole product rather than an option that has been added on afterwards. The tiers escalate on the number of professionals and on the volume of texts and email blasts included. It appears on medspa shortlists about as often as it appears on salon shortlists, which is a reasonable signal about where the product depth actually sits. Key features Per-location scheduling, reporting, and staff permissions

Client messaging with included text and email allowances that scale by tier

Forms as a paid add-on for intake and consent, which matters for treatment-led businesses

Integrations including QuickBooks as a paid add-on Pricing: Essentials is $176 a month per location, or $140 with annual billing, and covers up to 5 professionals with 100 texts, 500 email blasts, and 25 GB of storage. Premier is $293, or $234 annually, and lifts that to unlimited professionals, 250 texts, and 1,000 email blasts. Prestige is $410, or $328 annually, and adds the forms add-on with 2,500 texts and 10,000 email blasts. Enterprise pricing is quoted on request. Forms is $65 a month; QuickBooks is $45 a month. Rating: 4.6 on Capterra from 389 reviews. Where it falls short: the price. Two locations on Essentials is $280 a month at least, and the entry tier stops at 5 professionals, which many two-site salons will pass quickly. Card processing rates are not published on the pricing page, so you will have to ask for them before you can compare the real cost against the platforms that do publish. 4. GlossGenius Best for: solo stylists and small teams that want one flat price with card processing included in it. Solo stylists and small teams are the audience here, and the pricing reflects that. The Standard plan is $24 a month billed annually and includes the booking site, client notifications, email and text marketing, inventory and retail, and packages and memberships, with card processing at a flat 2.6 percent. For a one-chair business, that is a straightforward number to plan against. Key features Custom booking website with unlimited client notifications

Email and text marketing included from the entry plan

Inventory, retail, packages and memberships

Forms and waivers, Google booking, automated waitlist, and room and resource management from the Gold plan Pricing: Standard is $24 a month, Gold is $48 a month, and Platinum is $148 a month, all billed annually. Medspa plans are separate at $148 and $248 a month. Card processing is a flat 2.6 percent with no extra charge for tap-to-pay or card on file; instant payouts cost 1.8 percent, and the payroll add-on is $40 a month plus $6 a seat. The free trial is 14 days with no credit card. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 349 reviews. Where it falls short: the features a spa needs are not on the cheap plan. Room and resource management, automated waitlist, and forms and waivers all start on Gold at $48 a month, which is double the headline price. If you are a hair salon, the Standard plan may well be enough; if you have treatment rooms, it probably is not. 5. Fresha Best for: salons that want marketplace demand and are willing to pay a commission for the new clients that marketplace sends them. With Fresha, the subscription price is not the figure that decides what you pay in a year. Fresha charges $19.95 a month for an independent professional and $14.95 per team member per month for a team, which is genuinely low, and it then takes a 20 percent one-time commission on every new client who books through the Fresha marketplace, with a minimum fee of $6 per client, while returning clients are free. That commission is a customer acquisition channel with a price attached to it, and our view is that it gets misread as free software more often than any other pricing arrangement in this category. Key features Marketplace exposure to consumers searching for salons in your area

Subscription priced per team member rather than per location

Card processing built in, with buy now pay later available through Klarna

Optional add-ons for loyalty, insights, review generation, and an AI concierge Pricing: Independent is $19.95 a month, Team is $14.95 per team member a month, and enterprise pricing is quoted on request. The new-client marketplace commission is 20 percent with a $6 minimum per client. Online card payments are 2.79 percent plus $0.20; in-person payments are 2.29 percent plus $0.20 with an extra 10 cents for tap-to-pay, and manual card entry is 3.30 percent plus $0.20. Add-ons include client loyalty at $59.95 a month per location, insights at $9.95 per bookable team member, and an AI concierge at $99.95 a month per location. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 1,447 reviews. Where it falls short: the commission is charged on new clients, which means the cost of the platform rises exactly when the business is growing. If most of your new bookings already come from your own site, your own social accounts or word of mouth, you are paying a marketplace rate for demand you generated yourself, and you should model that before you switch. 6. Vagaro Best for: mixed beauty and wellness businesses where several different kinds of providers share one roof and one booking system. Vagaro has been in this market a long time, and it shows in the breadth of the feature list and in the size of the review base, which is over 3,600 on Capterra. The entry price is low and the platform scales by the number of bookable calendars rather than by location, which suits mixed businesses where hair, nails, massage and fitness share a roof. Key features Booking, calendars and client records for beauty, wellness and fitness businesses in one system

Website builder, marketing tools and a branded client app available in the subscription

Merchant services with a card reader included on sign-up

Pricing tiers selected by the number of bookable calendars, from one up to seven or more Pricing: the published rate is $23.99 a month as an introductory price for the first six months, with a standard price of $30.00, and the plan cost rises as you add bookable calendars. The free trial is 30 days and covers all features except email marketing, text marketing and the branded app. Card processing rates are quoted through Vagaro merchant services rather than published on the pricing page. Rating: 4.7 on Capterra from 3,651 reviews. Where it falls short: the trial excludes email marketing, text marketing and the branded app, which are three of the things a salon is most likely to be evaluating. You can trial the calendar but not the growth tools, so the first real test of those happens after you are already paying. 7. Square Appointments Best for: salons that already take payment on Square hardware and want the booking calendar attached to the till. There is a free tier here, and for a solo stylist who already takes payments on Square hardware it is a reasonable place to start, because booking is attached to the till and the reporting is one system rather than two. The paid tiers are priced per location and they also buy down the card processing rate, which is unusual and worth doing the arithmetic on if your card volume is high. Key features Online booking site, integrations, appointment reminders and unlimited staff calendars on the free plan

Cancellation policy, no-show fees, multi-staff appointment booking and a waitlist on the Plus plan

Future bookings report, service cost tracking and resource management on the Premium plan

Booking, payments, and reporting in one account with Square point of sale Pricing: Square Free is $0 a month, Square Plus is $49 a month per location, and Square Premium is $149 a month per location. In-person card processing is 2.6 percent plus 15 cents on Free, 2.5 percent plus 15 cents on Plus, and 2.4 percent plus 15 cents on Premium. Online payments are 3.3 percent plus 30 cents on Free and 2.9 percent plus 30 cents on the paid plans. Paid plans include a trial period. Rating: 4.5 on Capterra from 260 reviews. Where it falls short: the free plan is thin in the places where salons actually lose money. Cancellation policies, no-show fees, and the waitlist all require Plus at $49 a month per location. Payment processing is also Square-only, so if you have a processing rate you like elsewhere, you cannot bring it with you. 8. Acuity Scheduling Best for: single-service providers, mobile therapists, and small studios that need a scheduler rather than a salon management system. Acuity Scheduling is a scheduling tool that a lot of beauty professionals use, rather than a salon management system that happens to schedule. It is owned by Squarespace; the calendar and intake side is well built, and it is priced by the number of calendars you need rather than by staff or by location. For a single-service provider, a small studio or a mobile therapist, that is often the right shape. Key features Client self-scheduling with unlimited services and appointments on every plan

Payments through Stripe, Square, PayPal, and Venmo

SMS reminders, packages, and gift certificates from the Standard plan

HIPAA business associate agreement and custom API and CSS access on Premium Pricing: Starter is $16 a month billed annually or $20 monthly and includes 1 calendar. Standard is $27 annually or $34 monthly and includes up to 6 calendars. Premium is $49 annually or $61 monthly and includes up to 36 calendars. The free trial is 7 days and does not require a credit card. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 5,758 reviews. Where it falls short: it is a scheduler, and the salon-specific layer is not the centre of the product. There is no retail-first design, and the trial is only 7 days, which is short if you intend to import a client list, build a service menu, and test a real week of bookings before you decide. What to compare besides the booking calendar Most feature grids in this category compare the same eight things, and most of those eight are now table stakes. These are the areas where the platforms above genuinely differ. Online booking and per-staff calendars Every platform here will publish availability and take a booking. What varies is whether the system understands that a service is tied to a specific person with specific hours, that some services can only be performed by some staff, and that two stylists cannot occupy the same station. If you have more than two people, ask to see double-booking prevention configured, not described. Deposits, Cancellation Windows and No-Show Fees This is the group of settings that has money directly attached to it, and it is the group where the detail is worth checking carefully. A workable configuration will let you require a deposit or full prepayment on selected services, hold a card on file for the rest, define a cancellation window, and then charge the fee automatically when somebody cancels inside that window. Note that once you store a card to charge a late-cancellation fee later, you are handling payment account data. The standards for that are set by the card industry's security council, which was founded in 2006 by the major payment brands, and compliance is a question you should be asking your software vendor rather than assuming. Client Self-Service: Rescheduling, Cancelling And The Waitlist Self-service is the feature that removes phone calls, and it has two halves. The first is that a client can move or cancel a booking from the confirmation email or a client area without calling the salon. The second is that when a slot is released, the system automatically offers it to a waitlist rather than leaving a hole in the day. Plenty of platforms do the first. Fewer do the second, and on some of them the automated waitlist sits on a higher tier, so check which plan it is on before you price the system. Memberships, Packages And Gift Vouchers If you sell a six-session package or a monthly membership, the software has to track the balance, the expiry and the recurring charge, and it has to do that at the point of booking rather than in a spreadsheet afterwards. Gift vouchers are a separate question again, particularly for multi-site businesses, because the rules about where a voucher can be redeemed differ by platform. The Layer Beyond Booking: Point Of Sale, Retail And Staff Commission For a hair salon with a retail shelf and a commission structure, the booking calendar is maybe half the job. Point of sale, inventory, and commission tracking on both services and product sales are the parts that decide whether you are running one system or three. Mangomint and Boulevard are built with that layer in mind; the lower-priced schedulers generally are not, and that is a fair reason for the price gap. Client Apps And Staff Apps These are two different things, and they get conflated. A client app is a booking app your customers install, and it is mostly a retention and rebooking tool. A staff app is what your team uses to see their own schedule, check a client note before a service, and take a payment on the floor. Some vendors charge for one or the other, and a branded client app is frequently an add-on rather than an inclusion. Integrations The list to check is short and specific: your calendar (Google, Outlook, iCal or Office 365), your payment processor, your accounting package, and your email marketing tool. If a platform forces its own payment processing, that is not automatically bad, but it does mean the card rate is part of the subscription decision rather than separate from it. The Pricing Model, Which Is Where Most Of The Money Is Three models are in use across the eight platforms above, and they behave very differently as a business grows. A flat tier priced on staff count and booking volume is predictable, and it does not cost you more in a month when trade is good. The second model, a base fee plus a per-user charge, is manageable at three people and gets expensive at twelve, because the per-user line is charged whether or not that person is generating bookings. The third model, a commission on new clients, is inexpensive while you are quiet and increasingly expensive while you are growing, which is the opposite of what most owners assume when they sign up. Salons are small businesses in the statistical sense as well as the everyday one, since by the federal government's own count 99.9 percent of businesses are small, and at that scale a $10 per-user line item is not a rounding error. Build the twelve-month total under each model with your real numbers before you compare feature lists. Solo, Single-Site Or Multi-Location Changes The Answer For a solo stylist or a single mobile therapist, the calendar is the product, and almost everything else is overhead. GlossGenius, Acuity Scheduling, and the free Square Appointments tier all make sense at that size, and paying $130 a month for inventory and payroll you do not use is a poor trade. For a single location with three to ten staff, the decision usually comes down to whether you need the retail and commission layer. If you do, Mangomint and Boulevard are the serious candidates and the cost is justified. If you do not, a flat-tier platform such as Bookeo or a per-calendar platform such as Vagaro will cover the same booking workload for a fraction of the monthly cost. For multi-location businesses, ask one blunt question early: what exactly is shared between sites, and what is not. Some platforms give you one account with several locations inside it and consolidated reporting. Others, including Bookeo with its portal model, run each branch as a separate account with its own customers, staff, reports and vouchers, and give the portal manager access to each sub-account plus per-sub-account portal reports rather than a merged view. Neither approach is wrong. A franchise where each branch is independently owned often prefers the separated model, while a three-site group under one owner usually wants the consolidated one. What causes trouble is buying the first when you assumed the second, so get the vendor to demonstrate it on your own structure before you sign anything. Which One To Pick Naming one overall winner here would be tidy, and it would also be wrong, because the eight platforms are aimed at businesses of quite different sizes. Mangomint and Boulevard are the strongest choices when the business is large enough to need the full operations layer and can carry the monthly cost of it. For solo operators and very small teams, GlossGenius, Acuity Scheduling and the free Square Appointments tier are all sensible starting points. Fresha is a good arrangement if the marketplace is genuinely bringing you clients you would not otherwise have had, and a poor one if it is not, so that is the number to check first. Vagaro sits in the middle and tends to suit mixed beauty and wellness businesses that have several kinds of providers under one roof. If what you want is salon scheduling software with a predictable flat monthly cost, industry-specific booking rather than a general calendar tool, and no commission taken out of your bookings, Bookeo is built for that buyer, with the caveat about branch separation noted above. Whichever way you go, work out the twelve-month total under each pricing model using your own staff count and your own new-client numbers before you compare anything else. The feature lists across these eight platforms are fairly similar to one another. The annual invoices are not.

data.title: Vagaro Ranked Top Salon and Spa Management Software in G2 Summer 2026 Report
data.ai_summary: Vagaro was ranked top salon and spa management software in G2's Summer 2026 Spa and Salon Management Grid report, earning the highest overall position in the Leader quadrant. The ranking reflects over 53 million hair salon appointments scheduled on Vagaro in 2026, with a 4.6 out of 5 G2 rating.

industries.name: Personal Care & Wellness Booking Platforms (Beauty, Fitness, Spa)

data.full_text:
Vagaro Ranked Top Salon and Spa Management Software in G2 Summer 2026 Report
Vagaro Ranked Top Salon and Spa Management Software in G2 Summer 2026 Report
SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Vagaro, the leading platform for beauty, wellness, and fitness businesses, has been ranked the top salon and spa management software in G2’s Summer 2026 Spa and Salon Management Grid® Report.
"What makes this recognition especially meaningful is that it reflects the experience of the professionals who use Vagaro to run their businesses every day," said Fred Helou, Vagaro CEO.
Share
Vagaro earned the highest overall position in the report’s Leader quadrant, reflecting strong customer satisfaction and market presence. The ranking reinforces Vagaro’s position as an all-in-one software platform designed to help beauty and wellness businesses manage appointments, payments, clients, marketing, and day-to-day operations while supporting long-term growth.
In 2026 alone, over 53 million hair salon appointments were scheduled on Vagaro, a signal of the volume of business relying on the software daily and the clients booking through it.
Why do Salon and Spa Professionals Choose Vagaro?
The Summer 2026 ranking reflects feedback from the salon owners, spa professionals, stylists, estheticians, front desk teams, and business operators using platforms like Vagaro every day.
Vagaro currently holds a 4.6 out of 5 rating on G2, with hundreds of verified customer reviews highlighting strengths, including ease of use, online booking, appointment scheduling, client communication, deeply integrated AI, payment processing, marketing capabilities, and customer support.
"What makes this recognition especially meaningful is that it reflects the experience of the professionals who use Vagaro to run their businesses every day," said Fred Helou, Vagaro CEO. "Our focus has always been on building technology that helps beauty and wellness businesses operate more efficiently, deliver better client experiences, and create more opportunities for growth. Being ranked at the top of G2’s Summer 2026 report is a strong validation that we’re delivering on that."
What Makes Vagaro Salon and Spa Software Different?
Salon and spa professionals need more than appointment scheduling software. They need technology that supports the full client journey and the operational side of running a business without requiring multiple disconnected systems.
Vagaro brings those functions together on one platform.
Online booking operates 24/7 across a business’s website, the Vagaro Marketplace, and social channels, giving clients multiple ways to discover services and schedule appointments. Vagaro Merchant Services allows businesses to process payments through the same system they already use to manages appointments, helping connect tips, service charges, and retail sales to the rest of their operations.
Client records, appointment history, notes, SOAP notes, and preferences are also safely stored within Vagaro to help professionals maintain continuity across visits, giving them a more complete view of the client relationship.
For salons and spas managing a team, Vagaro also includes tools for payroll, commission tracking, and booth rental accounting. For independent professionals, Vagaro is more than flexible enough to support a single-person operation without adding unnecessary complexity.
Should any businesses be ready to invest in their next stage of growth, Vagaro Capital provides access to revenue-based financing that can help support important moves and expenses such as new equipment, additional space, or team expansion.
By bringing booking, payments, client management, payroll, marketing, funding, and reporting into one system, Vagaro helps beauty and wellness professionals by removing the need for multiple software subscriptions and minimizing the manual work of moving information between separate platforms.
How does Vagaro Continue to Invest in Salon and Spa Businesses?
As the needs of salons and spas continue to evolve, Vagaro remains focused on building technology that helps businesses operate more efficiently, deliver stronger client experiences, and grow with greater confidence.
The Summer 2026 ranking reflects that focus and the feedback of the professionals using Vagaro to run their businesses every day.
About Vagaro
Vagaro is the leading salon, spa, and fitness software, serving hundreds of thousands of professionals worldwide. Vagaro simplifies business management, credit card and payment processing, and makes it easy for businesses to grow their clientele on a modern consumer marketplace. Vagaro's a-la-carte options and affordable pricing provide a unique level of scalability, making it suitable for businesses of all sizes, from the solopreneur to enterprise franchises. Simple, innovative, and reliable, Vagaro empowers beauty and wellness professionals to excel in a digital age.

data.title: Vagaro Partners with bex+Co. to Power Booking, Payments, and Discovery for Independent Stylists Across Its Shared Workspace Salon™ Locations
data.ai_summary: Vagaro partnered with bex+Co. to provide booking, payments, and discovery tools for independent stylists across bex+Co. locations. Vagaro helped hair professionals acquire over 2.7 million new clients in the past 12 months. The partnership includes a unified stylist directory and access to Vagaro's marketplace.

industries.name: Personal Care & Wellness Booking Platforms (Beauty, Fitness, Spa)

data.full_text: SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Vagaro, the leading software platform for beauty, wellness, and fitness businesses, today announced a partnership with bex+Co.®, the Shared Workspace Salon™ built to support independent beauty professionals. Vagaro helped hair professionals acquire more than 2.7 million new clients over the past 12 months. Share The partnership brings together two companies focused on giving beauty professionals greater ownership over their businesses. Through Vagaro, bex+Co. professionals will have access to technology designed to help them manage and grow their businesses, including a new and unified stylist directory that will make it easier for clients to discover and book independent professionals across bex+Co. locations. The partnership is built on a shared belief that independence and support should go hand in hand, giving professionals the tools and visibility they need to grow on their own terms. What Do Independent Stylists Get Through the Vagaro and bex+Co. Partnership? Independent beauty professionals are responsible for much more than delivering a great service. They are also managing their schedules, attracting new clients, building loyalty, processing payments, marketing their businesses, and creating experiences that keep clients coming back. Vagaro brings those functions together within one platform, giving bex+Co. professionals tools for online booking, scheduling, payments, client management, marketing, reporting, and more. Just as importantly, Vagaro gives professionals additional opportunities to be discovered and get booked. Through the Vagaro Marketplace, businesses can reach a network of more than 52 million potential clients, creating another path for independent professionals to connect with new customers and turn discovery into appointments. For bex+Co. professional stylists and independent pros, that means the freedom to continue operating their businesses independently while gaining access to technology designed not only to simplify day-to-day operations, but to support long-term business growth. In fact, Vagaro helped hair professionals acquire more than 2.7 million new clients over the past 12 months alone. How Do Clients Find and Book a bex+Co. Stylist? While each bex+Co. professional continues to own and operate their individual business, the partnership creates a more connected experience across the broader bex+Co. network. The new stylist directory, powered by Vagaro, will give clients a centralized place to explore bex+Co. locations, discover individual professionals, learn more about their services, and book directly with the professional who is right for them. The result is a digital experience that strengthens the larger bex+Co. brand without taking ownership away from the individual businesses operating within it. "Independent stylists want ownership over their businesses, but ownership shouldn't mean having to build every piece of the infrastructure themselves," said Fred Helou, CEO at Vagaro. "bex+Co. has created a model that gives hair professionals autonomy while still surrounding them with community and support. Vagaro allows us to extend that model digitally, giving these professionals the technology and visibility to help them attract clients, build stronger relationships, and grow." What Tools Do bex+Co. Stylists Get with Vagaro? The partnership also gives bex+Co. professionals access to the same Vagaro platform used by independent beauty, wellness, and fitness businesses around the world. Professionals can rely on Vagaro’s pricing model and robust feature selection to ensure they aren’t paying extra for tools they don’t necessarily need, while tailoring their experience to best fit their business model. Essentially, as independent hair professionals’ businesses grow, Vagaro’s tools grow alongside them. “Growing beauty professionals has always been at the heart of bex+Co., which is why partnerships with companies that believe in supporting independent business owners matter so much to us. Vagaro Rolls Out Smarter Med Spa Software to Connect Treatment Data With Revenue Share:

Vagaro, a widely used platform for medical spa, beauty, wellness, and fitness businesses, has rolled out new medical spa software upgrades aimed at turning everyday treatment data into measurable business value. The rollout centers on stronger SOAP Notes and Custom Fields, both built to be HIPAA compliant while tightening up clinical workflows across the platform. "Having access to all the information, transaction lists, and dashboards has helped us make critical business decisions throughout the quarters and years," said Bailey Ames, Co-Founder of Lash + Company, a leading med spa enterprise. As med spas scale up services, open new locations, and see growing patient volumes, documentation demands are climbing right along with them. Providers still need to move quickly without sacrificing accuracy or consistency. With nearly 4 million appointments booked through Vagaro so far this year, the company says it's building its updates directly around how providers actually work day to day. These latest changes tie together several stages of the patient journey — consultation, treatment documentation, product tracking, inventory, billing, and checkout — into one connected workflow, helping practices manage more information without sacrificing the patient experience. Upgraded SOAP Notes Bring More Depth to Treatment Documentation The revamped SOAP Notes give providers a more dynamic way to handle EMR charting. Practitioners can now capture before-and-after photos mid-treatment and use them to visually document procedures as they happen. Photos can be annotated to mark treatment areas, making it easier to flag injection points, laser zones, or spots needing follow-up. Providers can also tag products and quantities directly to specific areas in treatment images, creating a precise record of what was used where. That data flows back into Vagaro's core platform, sharpening clinical clarity and communication between team members. Because product assignments are tracked automatically and carried through to checkout, treatment documentation stays linked to billing and inventory in real time — helping practices cut down on missed charges and keep inventory numbers accurate. To speed things up further, the new SOAP Notes support reusable dot phrases, letting providers complete detailed notes faster while keeping documentation consistent across the practice. Custom Fields Strengthen Consistency in Patient Records Vagaro's Custom Fields feature has also been expanded, giving med spas more flexibility in how they capture and organize patient information. Practices can use it to collect details like allergies, medications, skin type, and treatment history right on intake and consultation forms, with everything stored directly in the patient profile. That standardization helps keep records consistent across providers and locations, which matters when patients see multiple practitioners over time. It also reduces the odds of important details slipping through the cracks and makes information easier to find and review later. Because Custom Fields can capture key details before an appointment even starts, providers spend less time gathering information during the visit itself — freeing them up to focus on treatment and the overall patient experience. Connecting the Treatment Room to the Business Side Together, the enhanced SOAP Notes and Custom Fields create a more unified workflow — linking patient intake and treatment documentation with product management, injectable tracking, inventory, digital consent forms, and checkout. That gives providers a fuller picture of each treatment and everything tied to it. For multi-location med spas, this can mean more operational consistency across sites; for smaller, independent practices, it's a way to streamline daily workflow without added complexity. Either way, the platform is designed to keep documentation accurate and HIPAA-compliant while supporting the everyday balance between patient care and business needs. "These features are designed to reflect how med spas actually work," said Vagaro CEO Fred Helou. "By connecting what happens in the treatment room directly to inventory and checkout, we're helping practices protect their patients, improve accuracy, save time, and operate more effectively." Vagaro says it plans to keep building out tools tailored specifically to med spas, serving everything from small independent practices to larger enterprise operations. The goal, according to the company, is to help providers deliver strong patient care while giving them the operational tools to grow. With clinical documentation now more tightly connected to business operations, med spas using Vagaro can track treatment information, products, inventory, and checkout through a single, connected system a shift that's likely to matter more as the industry keeps expanding.

data.title: Vagaro's New Med Spa Software Is Real. The Problem for Investors Is That the Company Isn't Public.
data.ai_summary: Vagaro announced enhanced SOAP Notes and Custom Fields for its medical spa software, targeting HIPAA-compliant documentation and billing accuracy. The company, private and unlisted, serves over 100,000 businesses with estimated $66 million ARR. The med spa software market is projected to grow from $295 million in 2023 to $708 million by 2030.
data.author: Isaac Lanefollow

industries.name: Clinical Coding Support (ICD/CPT/SNOMED) & Documentation Compliance Tools

data.full_text:
On September 4, Vagaro announced two new features for its medical spa software platform — enhanced SOAP Notes and Custom Fields — and called them a way to turn treatment data into revenue. The announcement sounds like the kind of product ramp that, in a public SaaS company, might move the stock. Vagaro isn't public. It is a private company that has not filed for an IPO, and ordinary retail investors have no ticker to buy.

That alone is the first thing to understand before treating this as an investment lead. But the second thing — why Vagaro is making this move at all, and what the market behind it looks like — is worth the attention. It reveals a real growth story in a niche that sits at the intersection of health care compliance, consumer beauty spending, and small-business software. Understanding it helps you read the sector more clearly, even if you can't own Vagaro itself.

What Vagaro actually built

The announcement centers on two HIPAA-compliant features for the medical spa segment of its platform. SOAP Notes lets providers capture before-and-after photos and mark treatment areas — injection points, laser zones, areas of concern. Practitioners can assign products and quantities to those marked areas, and the data carries automatically through to checkout, inventory, and billing. The idea is to close the gap between what gets done in the treatment room and what gets charged and tracked at the register.

Custom Fields lets med spas collect patient-specific data — allergies, medications, skin type, treatment history — through intake and consultation forms and store it in a central patient profile. Both features are designed to support consistency across providers and locations, reduce missed charges, and improve billing accuracy.

Vagaro said nearly 4 million med spa appointments were scheduled through its platform year-to-date as of the announcement.CEO Fred Helou framed the features as designed to reflect how med spas "actually work," helping practices protect patients, improve accuracy, save time, and operate more effectively.

From a product standpoint, this is a vertical play. Vagaro is trying to stitch together the two halves of a medical spa business: the clinical side with HIPAA documentation requirements, and the service-business side that lives on bookings, retention, and margins. Most platforms were built for one half or the other. A platform that handles both can lock in deeper adoption — and make switching more costly.

The market behind the move

The timing isn't arbitrary. The U.S. medical spa market was valued at roughly $7.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at a mid-teen compound annual rate over the next decade, driven by rising demand for non-invasive aesthetic procedures like Botox, fillers, and laser treatments. The broader global market is estimated to exceed $25 billion.Medical spas operate profit margins of 20% to 25%, with top performers reaching close to 40%.

Within that industry, the medical spa management software segment is smaller but growing fast. Research firms estimate the market at around $295 million in 2023, projected to reach roughly $708 million by 2030 — more than doubling over seven years. As med spas professionalize and adopt compliance requirements, the software they use to run daily operations becomes more mission-critical.

Vagaro itself serves over 100,000 businesses across beauty, wellness, and fitness.Founded in 2009 and based in Pleasanton, California, it raised roughly $163 million in cumulative funding, and achieved a $1 billion unicorn valuation in 2021 when FTV Capital led a funding round.Estimates from private-market trackers put its annual recurring revenue around $66 million in 2024. The company operates in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and the UK.

What investors can't ignore: Vagaro is private

Here is where the story diverges from a typical stock research piece. Vagaro has no ticker symbol. It has not filed for an initial public offering. Shares are not available on public exchanges. Private market platforms like Hiive allow accredited investors to express interest in buying or selling shares, but these transactions are illiquid, subject to company approval, and not accessible to the average retail investor.

There is no public financial filing to examine, no earnings call to parse, no balance sheet to stress-test. The revenue estimates you'll find online — such as the $66 million ARR figure — come from third-party trackers, not company disclosures. The $1 billion to $2.5 billion valuation range cited by private-market databases is inferred from funding rounds and secondary activity, not from a market price.

For a retail investor, that means Vagaro itself is not an actionable investment. Any article that leads with a product announcement from a private company and doesn't address this constraint is skipping the first question you should ask: can I actually invest in this?

What the sector tells you about publicly traded alternatives

The med spa software market is too niche to support many publicly traded pure-players. Vagaro's closest competitor by category is Mindbody — which went public in 2015, was taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2019 for $1.9 billion, and reportedly plans a return to public markets. No public offering has materialized as of this writing.

That leaves investors looking at broader SaaS comparables in the business-software space — companies that serve appointment-based, service businesses more generally. The dynamics are instructive. Public SaaS multiples have compressed significantly across the board, creating a gap between private-market valuations and public-market pricing. The companies that command premiums in public markets are the ones showing revenue acceleration, expanding margins, and clear paths to free cash flow.

The question for any publicly traded name in this space is the same one that applies to Vagaro's strategy: does the platform's growth story have evidence behind it, in revenue acceleration, customer retention, margin expansion, and whether new product claims convert to measurable demand? Or is the company relying on narrative — that the med spa market is growing, therefore the software built for it must follow?

The investor takeaway

Vagaro's announcement is a genuine product expansion into a clinically regulated, fast-growing vertical. The features address a real operational gap in medical spa management — the friction between clinical documentation and billing — and the strategy of integrating both halves of the business makes sense.

But for the ordinary investor, the practical lesson is different. Product announcements from private companies tell you where the market is heading, not where you can invest. The med spa software market is growing, and the software layer within it is doubling in size over the next five years. That's a sector trend worth watching. Whether it translates into an investment opportunity depends on whether a company in this space goes public and whether, at that point, its growth, margins, and valuation support the multiple the market assigns.

Until then, the most useful thing you can do is pay attention to the dynamics — software adoption in professional services, the growing compliance burden on small health-adjacent businesses, and the competitive positioning of platforms that serve them. These are the variables that will matter when the next company in this space files for an IPO, and they may already be shaping the valuations of the publicly traded SaaS names you can own today.

Integrated booking enables deposits at booking, no-show fees from a stored card, automatic reminders, and one-tap rebooking at checkout, which directly protects revenue and retention. Spa management software emphasizes the service side — intake forms, treatment notes, packages, memberships, and room scheduling — while a POS emphasizes checkout, payments, tips, and retail. Accessed June 2026. 5 Common Mistakes Mobile Groomers Make When Choosing Software After talking with hundreds of service business operators, we’ve seen the same software selection mistakes repeat across industries. Mobile pet grooming is no exception. 1. Choosing based on advertised price instead of all-in monthly cost. A $23.99/mo platform becomes $60–$80/mo once you add the digital intake forms, text marketing, two-way messaging, and reputation management that your operation actually needs. Always request a fully itemized monthly cost based on your expected usage before signing a trial. The Small Business Administration consistently notes that hidden recurring costs are among the top financial surprises for small service business operators. 2. Prioritizing grooming-specific features over mobile-first usability. The most detailed pet profile system in the market is useless if accessing it on your phone between grooms takes 12 taps and a lag. Mobile groomers run their business from a phone, not a desktop. Every workflow — booking a rescheduled appointment, pulling a client’s vaccination notes, sending a “running 15 minutes late” text — must be fast and frictionless on a 5-inch screen. Test this specifically on your actual device during the free trial, not in a demo recording. 3. Not accounting for SMS volume when comparing platforms. A mobile groomer who sends 100+ texts per day — arrival notifications, “your pup is ready,” rebooking confirmations, review requests — can pay $15–$30/month in metered SMS overages on platforms that charge per message. On a $40/mo platform, that’s a 37–75% real price increase. Platforms with unlimited SMS (QuoteIQ, Groomer.io) eliminate this variable cost entirely. When comparing costs, always estimate your monthly text volume and calculate the true communication cost. 4. Picking a platform with no upgrade path. The software that works for a solo groomer with 40 clients often falls apart at 120 clients or 2 vans. Before committing, map out what happens when you hire your first part-time groomer. Does the platform charge per user? Does multi-van routing require a plan upgrade? Is the feature set you need at scale priced within reach? According to research from the IRS Small Business Tax Center, the average service business changes software once within its first three years — often because the initial platform couldn’t scale. Avoid the migration cost by choosing ahead of your current needs. 5. Evaluating software without testing the client experience. Your clients interact with your software every time they receive a reminder, book an appointment, or pay an invoice. A clunky booking portal loses you new clients before they’ve ever met you in person. During your trial, go through the complete client journey: book an appointment as a test client, receive the automated reminders, pay a test invoice, and submit a rebook request. If any step feels confusing or unprofessional from the client side, your clients will feel it too. Mobile Pet Grooming Software: What to Expect in the Second Half of 2026 The mobile pet grooming software market is moving fast. Three trends are actively shaping which platforms will matter most heading into 2027. AI-assisted booking and client communication are becoming standard expectations, not differentiators. Platforms that can automatically draft rebooking messages, flag clients who haven’t returned in 6 weeks, and send personalized “happy birthday to your pup” messages are pulling ahead in retention metrics. QuoteIQ’s AI Autopilot is one of the cleaner implementations of this at the SMB price point; MoeGo’s abandoned booking recovery is grooming-specific and effective. Expect more platforms to add AI communication features by Q4 2026. Subscription and membership models for grooming are gaining traction — particularly for high-frequency clients on a 4–6 week grooming schedule. According to SchedulingKit’s 2026 industry data, grooming businesses offering subscription plans see significantly better cash flow predictability and client retention than appointment-only models. Software platforms that support recurring billing and subscription management will have a meaningful advantage for mobile groomers trying to build a stable revenue base. Route optimization is moving from premium to standard. Two years ago, dedicated multi-stop route optimization was a feature only found on enterprise or specialized platforms. In 2026, it’s available at the $49/mo tier on MoeGo and built into QuoteIQ’s core platform. Groomers who are currently planning routes manually — whether that means drag-and-drop or just guessing — are leaving real money in inefficiency. The Mordor Intelligence market report projects that mobile/at-home grooming will grow at an 8.35% CAGR through 2031 — which means the operational efficiency advantages of route-optimized scheduling will compound meaningfully over the next five years.
