data.full_text:
Yelp Launches the New Yelp Assistant in Spring Release
Yelp launched its Spring Product Release with more than 35 new features and updates, including the new Yelp Assistant, an AI-powered chatbot that delivers instant answers, reliable recommendations, and seamless booking in one conversation.
New integrations with Vagaro, Zocdoc and Calendly expand scheduling capabilities across more categories on Yelp, while enhancements to AI-powered Menu Vision make deciding what to order more visual and engaging. The release also introduces new tools for advertisers, including an AI-powered support chatbot and enhanced advertising tools.
"The new Yelp Assistant is our most significant AI product evolution yet as we reconceive Yelp around instant answers and seamless actions," said Craig Saldanha, chief product officer at Yelp, in a statement. "The experiences and opinions from real people that power every recommendation are what sets Yelp Assistant apart, delivering trustworthy results that help consumers make confident decisions, faster. And for the first time, consumers can seamlessly move from discovery to action in a single conversation with new and enhanced integrations, from booking a table to ordering delivery or scheduling an appointment. As we transform Yelp with AI, this is only the beginning of a more conversational, personalized, and action-oriented Yelp experience."
First introduced to help consumers hire services professionals and answer questions about individual businesses, Yelp Assistant now works across every category on Yelp and is accessible at the center of the app through a new "Assistant" tab on iOS and Android. Powered by hundreds of millions of reviews, photos and detailed business information from the Yelp community, Yelp Assistant can handle complex and highly specific requests and surfaces real user-generated content from first-hand experiences in answers to validate each recommendation.
The new integrations available through Yelp Assistant are now also accessible throughout the Yelp app and include the following:
- Vagaro: Consumers can now book beauty and wellness appointments, such as haircuts, massages, and nail services.
- Zocdoc: Consumers can go from finding to booking a doctor on Yelp.
- Calendly: Service professionals can now connect their Calendly schedules to Yelp, allowing consumers to book consultations and appointments.
Additional features and updates from Yelp's 2026 Spring Product Release include the following:
- Enhanced Menu Vision that now overlays photos of dishes, drinks, and desserts directly over text-based menus when viewed through diners' phone cameras. "Popular" badges call out standout items, and with one tap, consumers can read reviews about the item. Plus, expanded coverage and improved matching accuracy mean more items are recognized across more restaurants. Menu Vision is available on iOS and Android from business media galleries or directly from business pages under the menu section.
- A more personalized and engaging home feed on iOS now surfaces more relevant, tailored content, more updates from people users follow, immersive full-screen videos and smarter nearby recommendations.
- Smarter photo discovery with natural language search within business media galleries.
- AI-powered chat support for advertisers that helps business owners get answers and resolve issues faster. Built with advanced large language models, the chatbot delivers conversational assistance across a wide range of support topics and provides intelligent real-time solutions.
- New tools to help businesses manage leads and optimize their advertising.

Don't want to read all those restaurant reviews or book a reservation yourself? Yelp is launching a new AI-powered assistant that you can use to ask questions and schedule services in one conversation.

The new AI assistant works across every category on Yelp and is available on both iOS and Android.

Yelp is the latest platform to bring agentic artificial intelligence -- AI models that can perform tasks on your behalf based on a conversational command -- into real-life services. Google has been giving Gemini more and more ability to take steps like calling businesses or booking trips for you, while integrating the chatbot deeper into systems like its Chrome browser. OpenAI's ChatGPT can do things like customize a Starbucks order or plan a Little Caesars pizza party. Then there are more advanced AI agents, like OpenClaw, which can take control of much of your digital life.

"The new Yelp Assistant is our most significant AI product evolution yet as we reconceive Yelp around instant answers and seamless actions," Craig Saldanha, chief product officer at Yelp, said in a statement. "And for the first time, consumers can seamlessly move from discovery to action in a single conversation with new and enhanced integrations -- from booking a table, to ordering delivery or scheduling an appointment."

Read also: Alexa Plus AI Can Order Food From Uber Eats and Grubhub, but Only With the Right Device

Get started with the AI-powered Yelp Assistant

You can now access Yelp Assistant at the center of the app through the new "Assistant" tab. The assistant uses the millions of evaluations, first-hand experiences, images and business details posted by Yelp users to execute complex tasks on your behalf.

Using the in-app AI assistant, you can reserve a table at any restaurant that uses Yelp Guest Manager for table booking, order takeout through DoorDash and Grubhub, request a quote for a service and book an appointment. You can reach out to professionals across hundreds of categories, such as auto, beauty, pet and event services, and book through integrations with platforms like Vagaro, Calendly and Zocdoc.

The company originally debuted its AI assistant in 2024, but these new features are an expansion to allow Yelp users to do more with the in-app chatbot.

data.full_text:
Yelp today announced more than 35 updates to its mobile app as part of a spring product release, including a more capable AI assistant that can now help initiate bookings and reservations.

The Yelp Assistant, launched in 2024, previously focused on answering questions about service providers and businesses. With today’s update, it now supports reservations, appointment bookings, quote requests, and takeout and delivery orders from the same chat interface.

Accessing the AI assistant is also easier; look for the dedicated tab on the homepage. You can provide the AI with as complex or specific prompts as you like, and it will scour relevant Yelp user reviews and ratings to deliver a precise yet personal response.

You May Also Like Keep Watching Artemis II’s Victor Glover: Flying Orion ’Was a Test Pilot’s Dream”

The idea is to show answers based on real-world experience, Yelp says. “There's a massive gap between how quickly people are adopting AI search and how much they actually trust it—research shows that few consumers greatly trust the results, and most want to see real reviews from real people, not just an AI-generated summary. Yelp Assistant was built to address this trust gap,” says Craig Saldanha, Yelp’s chief product officer.

You can ask Yelp Assistant to find a highly rated dentist, birthday spots with vegan options, and heated outdoor seating, or just to provide suggestions for an afternoon with your friends in a new city. When the assistant responds, you can ask follow-up questions or book an appointment or a table using the relevant links in the same chat interface.

Booking a dentist appointment via Yelp Assistant (Credit: Yelp)

The feature works for table booking at restaurants that use Yelp Guest Master, takeout and delivery orders on DoorDash and GrubHub, beauty and fitness appointments through Vagaro on iOS, healthcare appointments through Zocdoc on iOS, and auto-repair requests through RepairPal. You can also use the feature to request a quote for professionals in more than 450 categories, including home, auto, beauty, pet, and event services.

Yelp is also updating its Menu Vision feature. Now, when you hover your phone camera over a physical menu and point toward a particular dish, the feature will fetch user-uploaded photos and reviews of the dish.

These features start rolling out on Android and iOS today, with desktop rollout expected later this year. Check out Yelp’s blog post for an overview of all the other improvements it has made.

by [Kyt Dotson](https://siliconangle.com/author/kitdotson/)

SHARE

[Yelp Inc.](https://www.yelp.com/), the popular local business discovery and recommendation engine, today announced the launch of a new chatbot assistant alongside 35 new features and updates that will provide recommendations, answers, bookings and more. 

The company first introduced the Yelp Assistant to help customers hire service professionals and answer questions about individual businesses. Now it works across every part of the website. 

It lives in the “Assistant” tab on iOS and Android, and is powered by hundreds of millions of reviews, images, menus and detailed business information from the Yelp community. It can surface insights and handle complex questions and highly specific requests based on firsthand experiences. 

The assistant can also now go beyond merely providing information to take action on a customer’s behalf. “For the first time, consumers can seamlessly move from discovery to action in a single conversation with new and enhanced integrations — from booking a table to ordering delivery or scheduling an appointment,” Chief Product Officer Craig Saldanha said. 

Booking and ordering extend to numerous outlets and partnerships, the company said, including Vagaro Inc., Zocdoc Inc. and Calendly. Vagaro is a cloud-based beauty and wellness firm that allows consumers to book appointments such as haircuts, massages and nail services; with the assistant, users can soon find appointments at leading salons, spas and fitness outfits. Zocdoc provides an online healthcare marketplace that allows users to find in-network providers and book appointments instantly. 

“Booking a doctor’s appointment should be just as easy as booking dinner,” said Zocdoc founder and Chiff Executive Oliver Kharraz, M.D., adding that the integration with Yelp creates exactly that experience. 

### Enhancing the user experience

In addition to the Assistant, Yelp built in a broader user experience, with additional features including enhanced menus, a personalized home feed, smarter photo discovery and AI-powered chat support. 

Menu vision was introduced in 2025. It overlays photos of dishes, drinks and desserts directly over text-based menus when viewed through a phone camera. Menu items are ranked by popularity, and with a single tap, users can read community-generated reviews. The Yelp home feed on iOS now tailors relevant content to how users choose their recommendations, including immersive full-screen videos.  

Users can also use natural language to search for photos, helping them rediscover businesses and dishes that caught their attention.

data.title: Yelp’s updated AI assistant can answer questions and book a restaurant or service in one conversation
data.ai_summary: Yelp has launched an updated AI assistant that lets users ask questions, get restaurant reservations, order food delivery, and book service appointments all within a single conversational interface. The assistant integrates with external providers including DoorDash, Grubhub, Vagaro, ZocDoc, RepairPal, and Calendly to complete actions without leaving the app. The company is repositioning itself from a review platform to an "answers and action platform," hosting the assistant in a new central tab in its mobile app for iOS and Android.
data.author: Ivan Mehta

industries.name: Marketplace & On-Demand Platform Recommendations (rideshare, delivery, services)

data.full_text:
For years, existing consumer platforms have tried to keep users within their app by offering more services. After the rise of the AI chatbot, the trend is to have people use the assistant for both queries and actions without leaving the conversational flow. With its latest update, Yelp is letting people ask questions, get restaurant reservations, order food delivery, and book service professionals, all through its updated AI assistant. The company debuted the AI assistant in 2024 to help people search for different services based on their problem. It is now using the platform data paired with an AI assistant to let users do more tasks. In a demo seen by TechCrunch, the company’s SVP of product, Akhil Kuduvalli Ramesh, searched for hiking places to go with a dog without a leash; looked for takeout places along the way, with an option to place an order on Doordash; looked for restaurant recommendations for a weekend plan, with an option to check out availability and book a table; and queried about painting a friends’ new Victorian house without leaving the chat. “We would really like consumers to reconceive Yelp as a place where they can ask questions and get answers, not just that, but also complete the action. That’s Yelp reconceiving from a review platform to an answers and action platform,” he told TechCrunch over a call. “Some of the investments we’re making will be in that lane.” Users can select a specific page for a restaurant or service when they tap on it, or ask more questions about the business. Yelp said that as the knowledge is grounded in details of the business on the platform, the business’s website, and user reviews, there is a scant chance of getting wrong answers. The company is hosting the assistant in a new tab in the app, which is now placed in the center of the bottom navigation bar, so users are likely to visit it more often. The assistant will be available on iOS and Android at launch and will work with eligible business pages, including restaurants, retail shops, and attractions. The company said that the desktop version and rollout across all kinds of businesses are slated for later in the year. Apart from fetching information, Yelp also announced integration with external providers to complete an action, like place an order or appointment. Users can now order food through DoorDash and Grubhub, book fitness or beauty appointments through Vagaro, a doctor’s appointment through ZocDoc, and a car repair through Repairpal. Plus, it also offers a Calendly integration for other kinds of businesses that allow appointment booking. Techcrunch event Meet your next investor or portfolio startup at Disrupt

Kuduvalli mentioned that while the redirections are the way Yelp is set up now, it might not “remain that way” in the future. Besides the new AI assistant, Yelp is rolling out a few quality-of-life updates to the app. Last year, it launched the ability for people to scan a menu and see what dishes look like through photos other users posted. There is a new AI-powered personalization model for the Yelp home feed on the iPhone and iPad , and it is able to surface more relevant content and improved recommendations.

Yelp is also updating its AI Menu Vision feature with support for photo overlays so users can see what popular dishes, drinks, and desserts look like.

Frequently Asked Questions About Salon Booking Software What is salon booking software? Salon booking software is a digital system that allows salons to manage appointments, enable online client booking, send automated reminders, and connect scheduling to checkout and client management. Modern salon booking software replaces paper appointment books and telephone booking with automated, 24/7 digital systems that reduce no-shows and capture bookings outside business hours. How much does salon booking software cost? Salon booking software costs vary widely — from free plans (Fresha, Square Appointments free tier) to $20–50/month for solo operators (GlossGenius, Timely), $30–175/month for single-location salons (Vagaro, Boulevard), and custom enterprise pricing for multi-location chains (Zenoti, Phorest). Most platforms charge per location, per user, or as a percentage of bookings processed. Factor in transaction fees, hardware costs, and setup fees when comparing total cost of ownership. What is the best free salon booking software? Fresha previously offered a free base plan but has since moved to a subscription model — the Independent plan starts at $19.95/month and the Team plan is $14.95 per staff member per month. Square Appointments still offers a free single-user tier. For salons with an established client base, paid platforms typically become more economical than transaction-fee models above a certain monthly booking volume. Can salon booking software integrate with Google? Yes. Most leading salon booking software platforms — including Zenoti, Vagaro, Boulevard, and Phorest — integrate with Google Reserve, allowing clients to book directly from Google Search and Google Maps results. This is one of the most valuable integrations available because it captures bookings from clients who are actively searching for a salon in their area. What is the difference between salon booking software and salon management software? Salon booking software refers specifically to the appointment scheduling and client booking component. Salon management software is a broader term for an all-in-one platform that includes booking plus POS, CRM, inventory management, marketing automation, and reporting. Most modern platforms — including Zenoti — are full management platforms that include booking as one component of a complete, connected system. When should a growing salon move from a simple booking tool to a full management platform? The clearest signals are operational rather than size-based. Because BNPL services let customers break up their payments into smaller, interest-free installments, they provide a substitute for conventional credit cards. By giving those who would not be eligible for traditional credit cards or loans access to credit, BNPL services can aid in the promotion of financial inclusion. Shifting consumer preferences and economic anxieties BNPL services provide a practical substitute for traditional credit card debt as consumers grow increasingly suspicious of it and want more flexible payment choices. With these services, customers can spread out their payments over time rather than paying the entire amount once for their products. This is consistent with spending within a budget and avoiding high-interest loans. Economic uncertainties like unstable employment and income fluctuations also encourage customers to look for flexible payment options that don't put a load on their finances. Restraints Impact of credit score The increased reliance on digital gadgets for business, education, and leisure, along with new product releases and technological breakthroughs, contributed to a notable spike in consumer demand for electronic goods. Consumer debt and affordability A considerable amount of debt, including mortgages, credit card debt, and student loans, is already borne by many consumers. Opportunities Expansion of retail sector BNPL services, which enable customers to buy and pay for products in installments, have been linked to Internet shopping. News › AmSpa News, Medical Spa Show, News Aesthetic Technology and AI for Medical Spas: The Aesthetic Tech, Innovation & AI Summit at Medical Spa Show 2026 Med spa technology is advancing quickly. Electronic medical records, EMR, customer relationship management, CRM, lead management systems, LMS, automated marketing tools, AI assistants, and imaging platforms are reshaping how high performing aesthetic practices operate. The right tools help you book more of the right patients, protect your time, and deliver a safer, more consistent patient experience. That is why Medical Spa Show 2026 is introducing the Aesthetic Tech, Innovation & AI Summit, a full day deep dive into the software, systems, and AI innovations that can actually make your day to day easier, not more overwhelming. Thanks to innovative sponsors including Podium, Illume, Phorest Software, Medvelle, MarketStorm, The Data Co., Vagaro, Mega, and Boulevard, med spa professionals will get practical, vendor supported education on how to use technology effectively to serve patients, make data-informed decisions and grow their practices. Explore the pre-education deep-dive courses at Medical Spa Show 2026. Who Should Attend the Aesthetic Technology, Innovation & AI Summit If you are a busy medical spa owner or practice manager who suspects your technology could be doing more for you, this Summit is built for you. This full day pre-education featured session benefits any aesthetic professional looking to level up in 2026, including: Folks who are unfamiliar with the essential software needed to support aesthetic practice.

Demystifying and clarifying software roles – less acronyms, more understanding.

Operators, owners and administrators looking to update or improve their current software choices or utilization.

Those looking to be inspired by technology to work smarter not harder.

Those looking to do more with automation.

Those wanting to work with AI more in their practice. Next Gen EMR for Medical Spas Starter electronic medical record (EMR) systems may not have the functionality to grow with your aesthetic practice. Med spas often find difficulties customizing workflows, integrating with other operational systems and generating the report they need to make key business decisions. In this session, Podium shares what the Next-Gen EMRs can do for medical aesthetic practices and what successful implementation can do to support your team, patient experience and bottom line. Speed to Lead in Med Spas, Using a Lead Management System to Convert More Aesthetic Patients Why is “speed to lead” such a big deal in aesthetics? Because patients are often comparing multiple practices. If one office responds in five minutes and the other in two days, the decision is usually made long before either provider discusses treatment options. Missed calls, slow responses to website forms or Instagram DMs, and inconsistent follow-up can turn into lost leads and lost potential revenue for your medical aesthetic practice. A Lead Management System, LMS, is designed to plug those holes. An LRM can: Capture leads from your website, social media, call tracking, and other sources.

Alert your team quickly so someone can respond while the patient is still actively interested.

Track the status of each lead: new, contacted, consult scheduled, no show, converted, and more.

Automate follow-up using text or email when someone does not book right away or needs reminders. Med Spa CRM Systems, Turning Patient Data into Long Term Growth Many aesthetic practices confuse EMR and CRM. They do very different jobs. An EMR protects and organizes clinical information, and a CRM, Customer Relationship Management system, protects and organizes your relationship with the patient. A CRM lets you market smarter, with opportunity to personalize your outreach; you can send the right message to the right patients at the right time, automatically. For a medical spa, a CRM helps you: Keep all patient contact details, preferences, and interaction history in one place.

Manage appointment reminders, reactivation campaigns, and review requests.

Segment patients by treatment interest, birthday month, membership status, or spend level.

Run targeted marketing, for example, a gentle reminder to filler patients who are due for touch ups or to laser patients who are ready for their next series. Medical Spa Photography Technology, Improving Outcomes and Patient Education You know before and after photos are essential for aesthetics. They prove your results, display your aesthetic style, and drive word of mouth. The Photography session focuses on how the right tech can streamline and standardize this process within your med spa. Membership Software and Revenue Analytics for Med Spas, Making Income Predictable Cash flow can be unpredictable in aesthetic medicine. Demand for certain aesthetic treatments can be seasonal, such as with laser energy devices, where you might have a huge month followed by a slower one, even when patient satisfaction is high. Membership and loyalty programs, backed by accurate revenue and reporting tools, become essential. During the Revenue & Membership Programs session you will explore how to design a successful membership program that fits your patient base, supports predictable recurring revenue, and is easy for your team to administer. Roundtable Med Spa Software Demos, Hands On Learning With Industry Innovators Even once you understand the concepts, choosing specific tools can feel intimidating. What makes them different? Which tools make the most sense for a new vs. established practice, for solo practitioners or franchised clinics? The lunchtime Roundtable Software Demos at the Summit are designed to make this easier and much more practical. Instead of long sales presentations, you get the opportunity to sit at small tables with vendors whose tools you are actually curious about, and ask them your burning questions. Ask questions about their integrations, training, and support, and hear about how other owners and operators at your table are using, or evaluating, the same software. Med Spa Dashboards and KPIs, Seeing Your Aesthetic Practice at a Glance Most owners know they should be looking at their numbers more often but can become overwhelmed by spreadsheets and scattered reports. That is where a The Power of a Customized Dashboard comes in, a single screen that shows the metrics that matter most to your practice. With support from focused analytics, you and your practice manager can see how better visibility can turn your data into clear decisions about pricing, staffing, marketing, and service mix. The dashboard session focuses on: Identifying your true KPIs, new leads, conversion rate, show rate, average ticket, revenue per provider, membership growth, and more.

Designing a dashboard that tells you, in seconds, whether the month is on or off track.

Visualizing your key revenue funnels, from first inquiry through repeat booking. Virtual and Remote Teams for Med Spas, Expanding Capacity Without Overstaffing The Summit explores when remote roles make sense, and when they do not. It also goes into typical costs and how they compare to full time staff, along with how to set remote and virtual team members up for success. With the right processes and technology, Virtual & Remote Employees can effectively handle: Phone calls and scheduling.

Lead follow-up and recall campaigns.

Social media messages and website chat.

Back office tasks like inventory or basic bookkeeping. Automated Med Spa Marketing, Staying Visible Without Burning Out Many med spa owners find themselves doing “just one more thing” after hours, writing emails, trying to remember who is due for Botox, and figuring out what to post on social. Automated Marketing is about building systems that keep your brand in front of patients. Learn more about: What can be automated, recall reminders, pre and post treatment education, reactivation messages for lapsed patients, birthday or anniversary offers, membership nudges, review and referral requests.

How to set up simple “journeys” that are triggered by events, consult completed, treatment performed, membership renewal approaching.

How to keep automation feeling personal by using patient names, specific treatment references, and realistic timing. Artificial intelligence in the med spa world is already showing up in very practical ways. The AI Options You Can Implement Now session focuses on every-day applications such as: Drafting patient education content or post care instructions you can review and customize.

Suggesting subject lines and social captions to speed up your marketing.

Helping categorize or prioritize leads based on behavior, who opened emails, clicked links, or visited key pages.

Surfacing patterns in your data, like which treatment combinations tend to generate the highest lifetime value. Future Med Spa Technology and AI Innovations, What Is Coming Next Beyond what is available right now, the Summit closes with a forward-looking discussion on Future Tech and AI Innovations to Watch for Medical Spas. Expect conversation around: More advanced analytics and predictive modeling, for example, forecasting demand by season or service.

Emerging imaging and diagnostic tools that enhance consultations and treatment planning.

Deeper integrations between platforms so the med spa patient experience feels seamless from first click to long term maintenance. Leave with a realistic sense of where aesthetic technology is heading, so you can make smart, staged investments instead of reactive ones. Salon POS System: Top 5 Software Picks for 2026 Table of Contents









Boulevard Blog Salon • Best Practice Salon POS System: Top 5 Software Picks for 2026 Best Salon POS Systems: Top 5 Software Picks for 2026 Table of Contents What Is a Salon POS System?

Features To Look for in a Salon POS System

How To Choose the Best Salon POS System

5 Best Salon POS Systems

Why Boulevard Is the Best Salon POS System

FAQ Ready to join Boulevard? Get a Demo Feb.13.2026 UPDATED . Jun.25.2026 BY Skya Jones Modern salons need point-of-sale (POS) systems that handle it all. The right system can seriously up your game by improving client interactions and boosting revenue . The best salon POS system does more than process payments. Modern salon POS software helps businesses manage appointments, client profiles, inventory, reporting, and retail sales from one platform When it’s easy to buy the products as they check out and book appointments from home, clients are more likely to rebook again and again. In this guide, we’ll give you the inside scoop on POS software, like what it can actually do for your salon and which are the best POS systems for salons in 2026. What Is a Salon POS System? Salon POS systems are central hubs for the front desk. These software-forward systems support the client experience as much as the salon’s checkout process. They combine software with hardware like iPads and card readers so your clients can easily pay for their visit (and any retail products they’re picking up). A salon POS system is purpose-built for beauty businesses and helps manage payments, appointments, inventory, and client relationships from a single platform. A POS system handles most of your salon’s financial tasks in one place, processing payments, calculating tips and loyalty discounts, and managing retail and reporting programs. Some even make it easy to integrate with other software that tracks staff hours and performance, leading to less manual work on your end. Features To Look for in a Salon POS System Shopping for salon POS software gets a lot easier when you know what to look for. Every self-care business is unique, but here are a few features that most teams need. When comparing salon POS software, prioritize tools that improve both client experiences and day-to-day operations. Fast and flexible checkout: POS software should make paying fast and convenient for everyone, offering things like mobile payment options and easy-to-follow on-screen prompts.

Integrated payments and tipping: Your POS system should support multiple payment options, like mobile wallets and cards on file, so no one has to dig through their wallet for the one method you accept. Look for software that automatically calculates tips at set percentages (like 15%, 20%, and 25%) and applies loyalty rewards and discount codes, too.

Reporting and sales insights: Good salon POS software doesn’t stop working for you once the client has paid. It’ll also include high-level details like retail trends and retention data . These insights can help you adjust your strategies (such as scheduling a full-team workshop to perfect the latest TikTok hairstyle trend) and stay on top of your revenue flow before rent’s due.

Client profiles and purchase history: Choose tools that let you personalize the salon experience. Client profiles store information like their birthdays for special discounts and notes from their past sessions to help your stylists provide better service from moment one.

Retail and inventory management: Keep track of backbar inventory and retail products directly in your POS system. Your software should send an alert when you’re running low and automate order purchasing so you never have to run out of a dye color mid-service. How To Choose the Best Salon POS System Before you start researching and selecting a POS system , you need a game plan. There are lots of software solutions for spas out there, so knowing what you need ahead of time can side-step information overload. These tips will help you stay organized and focus on your salon’s long-term goals. The right POS system for a beauty salon should support your current workflows while giving you room to grow. Define Your Salon’s POS Needs Choosing software starts with taking stock of your needs, so assess your current POS processes. What does the checkout process look like? Where does it slow down? Are there features that overlap with your other software solutions or things you’d like to collapse into one program? Make a list of your wants and needs, then reference it during your search to narrow down your options. Evaluate Ease of Use for Your Staff Your chosen POS software should make your employees’ lives easier. Ideally, they’ll be able to pick it up in their first few days without tons of hands-on training. Part of this onboarding process includes the software company’s customer service, too. A program with a strong team behind it will help you set everything up and get questions answered along the way. Check How the POS Connects To Booking and Scheduling The best POS tools integrate with scheduling systems you already use. Appointment reminders, automated calendar syncing, and easy rebooking options can reduce no-shows and double-booking. This way, your front desk team can schedule clients for a touch-up or a fresh cut in six weeks while they’re still standing at the counter, so they’re more likely to keep coming back . Compare Pricing and Total Cost Price is always important to consider, especially if you're just getting established or planning your next location. But comparing upfront costs is only the first step. You also need to compare how different software options impact your long-term overhead. Some systems may seem affordable at first, but consider how they’ll impact your overhead over time. Study the fine print: Are there high processing fees? Are their long-term contracts undercut by unreasonable cancellation penalties? POS systems that don’t integrate well with other software means paying for more subscriptions every month, too. Plan for Growth and Scalability You shouldn't have to adjust your business goals around your software or do a massive overhaul every time you outgrow your current system, no matter how big your salon gets. So make sure your beauty salon’s POS has the flexibility to scale with your growing salon. It should be able to manage more locations and team members without glitching, process more complex loyalty and membership programs, and have the wiggle room to add new workflows as tech evolves. 5 Best Salon POS Systems Every POS system has its strengths, but not all of them are going to be the right fit for your needs. The best salon POS systems vary based on your budget, team size, and operational needs. We’ve gathered details on five of the best POS systems for salons so you can cut the noise and find software that works for you. 1. Boulevard Boulevard is an all-in-one platform designed for premium salon management and client experiences. It is one of the best salon POS software solutions for growing salons that want scheduling, payments, reporting, and client management in one place. It’s an ideal choice for established and growing salons looking to streamline every workflow while maximizing their income. It integrates with over a dozen other common apps and web services while bringing everything else in-house. Some of Boulevard’s best features include: Flexible payment methods

Role-based permissions and staff management

Organized client profiles and inventory tracking

Multi-location management and reporting tools

Cross-device compatibility

Precise scheduling and self-booking portals

Integrated loyalty programs and marketing campaigns Pricing starts at $158/month/location for salons paying annually. 2. Vagaro Vagaro is a POS platform that’s generally used by independent stylists and small salons that also offer fitness and wellness classes. It includes a website builder and a marketplace where users can find salons in their area. Its notable features include: Hybrid salon and fitness POS management

Online booking and scheduling

Client discovery marketplace

Calendar synchronization

Vagaro-branded hardware that’s automatically compatible with their software For one stylist at one location, Vagaro starts at $23.99/month. Pricing scales with the number of stylists—with seven or more, you’ll pay $83.99/month. However, if you run more than one location, you’ll need to reach out to their support team for more information about their enterprise pricing. Vagaro also offers a 30-day free trial. 3. Mangomint Mangomint’s POS system is known for its simple interface, designed for independent salons and boutique spas looking for software without any frills. It’s mainly a POS software, but offers some lightweight marketing tools, booking portals, and client data storage options. Here are some of Mangomint’s main features: Self-checkout and tip prompts

Scheduling and staff management

Virtual waiting rooms

Two-way text-based client communication

Remote payments

Pricing starts at $175/month for small teams and includes a free trial. 4. Fresha Fresha is a low-price POS software with a focus on flexible scheduling and data privacy. It’s a budget-conscious option known for its app-based marketplace, similar to Vagaro. Fresha includes room for extensive client notes, making it a better option for medspas and boutiques that offer medically focused or detail-oriented services than traditional salons. This POS system’s core functions include: HIPAA compliance to protect client data

Centralized client app

Automated appointment reminders

Up-front payment options

Global currency support

Pricing starts at $19.95/month for a single provider, or $14.95/stylist/month for teams, with a seven-day free trial. If your salon has over 20 team members, you’ll need to reach out to Fresha’s support team for enterprise pricing details. 5. Square Square is a general business platform used by businesses of all kinds. Its salon-specific POS software includes marketing campaigns, scheduling apps, and multiple payment options, with a focus on the client experience. Since it’s a widespread software solution, clients are likely to be familiar with Square—but there are fewer UI customizations you can use to personalize the look to match your brand identity. Some of the major features of this POS system include: No-fee tier for solo stylists

Enterprise-level scaling capabilities

Color-coded staff scheduling and commission tracking

Inventory management Square offers a free plan for single salons, with only a few basic features. Richer experiences start at $49/month/location. Why Boulevard Is the Best Salon POS System The right POS system can reshape your salon’s client experience. With faster checkout, accurate tipping, and easy rebooking, your salon can keep the relaxing vibes going after clients walk out the door. Modern salons need modern software to stay on top of their schedules and keep their clients happy. Boulevard is an all-in-one platform that simplifies checkouts for self-care businesses of all sizes and supports you as you grow. Whether you’re looking at client profile management or financial reporting, bring everything together with our advanced software solution. Check out Boulevard's Salon Software to learn more. FAQ Does a salon POS system need to integrate with scheduling software? A POS system can stand on its own, but it can improve daily workflows when it’s integrated with scheduling tools. Adding appointment booking and calendars to your POS system can boost your client retention because it’s easier for front desk staff to book a client’s next appointment in the moment. Can a salon POS system track tips and commissions? Yes, and they should! Strong POS software can automatically calculate tips and offer set percentages that make it easier for clients to pick an appropriate amount. It can also track commissions for a more accurate picture of your finances. When should a salon consider upgrading its POS system? It might be time to upgrade if there are lines forming at your front desk due to error messages and lag, or if it isn’t compatible with the latest hardware and payment methods. Feeling like it’s time to update your other hardware and software systems is also an indicator that it’s time to look into a new POS system—or an all-in-one choice like Boulevard . What is the best salon POS system? Boulevard, Vagaro, Mangomint, Fresha, and Square are among the best salon POS systems available today. The right option depends on your salon's size, goals, and operational needs. How to Fill Your Schedule and Reduce No-Shows

Keeping your schedule full and minimizing missed appointments are two of the biggest challenges massage business owners face. If your calendar has gaps or you’re constantly chasing clients who don’t show up, you’re losing revenue and wearing yourself thin.

That’s where effective massage therapy booking software plays a pivotal role.

The guide includes detailed feature comparisons of nine competing platforms: Glofox, WellnessLiving, Vagaro, MarianaTek, Hapana, Zen Planner, Exercise.com, Momence, and Kenko, evaluating each on criteria such as consumer marketplace access, dynamic pricing, integrations, and customer support. The article serves as promotional content for Mindbody while providing a comprehensive comparison across the sports facility software category.

data.full_text:
Running a successful medical spa today means more than offering injectables or facials—it requires a seamless blend of clinical care, retail efficiency, and spa-level experience. Behind the scenes, your EMR is the backbone that keeps everything running smoothly.

Whether you're launching your first location or scaling a multi-room aesthetics practice, the right EMR empowers you to streamline scheduling, manage inventory, track revenue, and deliver a standout client experience—all while staying compliant.

What is a Med Spa EMR?

A Meds Spa EMR (Electronic Medical Record) is a digital system designed to document and manage clinical, operational, and administrative workflows in a medical spa. Unlike traditional EMRs used in primary care, med spa EMRs are tailored for aesthetics and wellness services—supporting everything from Botox injections and laser treatments to IV therapy and skincare consultations. These platforms often combine scheduling, charting, patient communication, inventory management, and billing in one easy-to-use interface.

Why Use a Med Spa EMR?

Using a medical spa EMR helps streamline daily operations, improve patient experiences, and maintain compliance with medical documentation standards. With features like real-time inventory tracking, automated charting templates, and integrated marketing tools, medspa EMRs can reduce administrative burdens while boosting profitability. Whether you're a solo injector or managing a multi-provider practice with additional services like redlight sauna or cold plunge, the right EMR can help you deliver consistent, high-quality care—and scale your business more efficiently.

Top 9 Medical Spa EMRs

In 2026, these are the top nine EMRs leading the way for medical spas:

OptiMantra

Custom templates for aesthetic, wellness, and medical services

Built-in scheduling, POS, and telehealth

Package and recurring memberships sales and tracking

Inventory management in beauty business 10 min Back to blog Best salon inventory management software (2026): pricing, pros & cons Written by Kir Fesenko CPO at Suplery 5+ years in software for beauty business, 5+ in UX/UI design, 3+ in web design He is open to communication on E-mail and LinkedIn. Edited by Alina Kamalova You didn’t open this guide because spreadsheets are your hobby. You opened it because you need one place to see what’s in stock, who used it, and what to reorder — before Friday turns into a supplier sprint and emergency ordering. Whether you’re sketching your opening-day checklist or already juggling a busy salon across multiple locations, the pain points are the same: sudden stockouts of bestsellers, cash stuck in slow moving products, messy inventory tracking, and too many “Did anyone order this?” moments. So here’s the plan — a tour of salon inventory management software that shows what actually matters day to day. We’ll compare tools head-to-head with real pricing, pros/cons, and best-fit use cases — with a spotlight on core functionality: clean stock counts and inventory tracking you can manage in just a few clicks, a booking system that plays nicely with your stock, and a salon POS system with integrated credit card processing that won’t slow checkout. Quick glossary as you read: backbar = professional-use supplies at the station; retail = products you sell to clients; POS= point of sale (checkout and payments); CRM = client records and notes; POs = purchase orders. The 3 types of “salon inventory software” (and why that matters) 1) General salon software suites (Vagaro, Square Appointments, Fresha, GlossGenius, Rosy, Zenoti, Boulevard) All-in-one platforms that combine online booking, appointment management, a salon POS system at checkout, CRM for client profiles, integrated marketing tools, and an inventory module. For most salon owners, this covers the core: inventory tracking, low-stock alerts, basic purchase orders, sometimes barcode scanning — plus automated reminders and Google Calendar sync to keep client appointments tight. 2) Specialized salon inventory tools (Suplery, Vish, SalonScale) Built to control backbar usage (the professional supplies used during services) and product cost. Vish and SalonScale pair with Bluetooth scales to weigh bowls and refine formulas; Suplery adds an in-app supplier marketplace so you track counts and place orders in just a few clicks. These tools turn waste into data and make parts-and-labor pricing straightforward. 3) General inventory / accounting systems (Intuit QuickBooks) Accountant-grade inventory management software for POs (supplier orders), valuation, COGS (cost of goods sold), and FIFO/FEFO (stock-rotation rules — first in/first out; first-expire/first-out) — powerful for financials, but not salon-workflow-native, so it’s often used alongside a salon suite. Desktop vs mobile (you’ll want both) Desktop is where managers set rules and run the numbers — reports, purchase orders, vendor terms, analytics, and catalog edits. Mobile/tablet is where the action lives — scan barcodes at the station, weigh bowls in the color room, log backbar usage, and run a quick stock count between clients. Modern salon inventory management software supports both so a busy salon can streamline operations without switching tools mid-shift. The 8 jobs your inventory tool must do Real-time stock levels for backbar / treatment rooms and retail Automated reordering — min/max, alerts, POs Per-service materials usage (grams/ml/units) to reduce waste across services Parts-and-labor pricing and true materials cost per service Analytics — turnover, ABC, shrinkage, sell-through, COGS Multi-site controls — transfers, permissions, parity across locations Lot / expiry tracking and FEFO where needed (skincare, tints, lash/brow adhesives, disposables, injectables) Team accountability — who used what, when (no more “did anyone order this?” moments) Want the fundamentals step by step? Frequently asked questions What is the best salon management software? There isn’t a single “best” — it depends on your shape. Example: you use 5 tubes/day, delivery takes 4 days, and you want 10 tubes of safety stock → 5×4 + 10 = 30. Set minimum at 30 and maximum near 60 so alerts and POs trigger on time. If demand is spiky, add a 10–25% buffer. Backbar vs retail — what’s different for inventory control and pricing? Backbar hits COGS per service and belongs in a parts-and-labor model: measure usage (grams/ml) and either bill transparently or bake it into service pricing. Retail drives top-line — you want clean SKUs, barcode sales, returns, bundles, and a faster inventory turnover. For backbar, weigh color bowls to stop over-mixing. For salon owners with multiple locations, add transfer volume and count accuracy by site. Tie client appointments and retail recommendations to KPIs to improve client retention. How do booking and inventory talk to each other? Your booking system should support online booking, appointment booking reminders, and ideally Google Calendarsync. Your salon inventory management software should update counts when products sell at POS and when you record backbar usage. Tools like Square or Vagaro let you add a booking widget to your website and ring retail at checkout, while a usage tool (Vish/SalonScale) keeps the color room honest. data.title: 7 Fresha Alternatives: Specialized Booking Solutions for Salons and Spas In 2026
data.ai_summary: This article is a curated buyer's guide comparing Fresha, a cloud-based booking platform serving over 130,000 beauty and wellness businesses, with seven specialized alternatives for salon and spa scheduling software in 2026. The alternatives include Salon Booking System (WordPress-native, zero commissions, annual pricing from €89/year), Zenoti (enterprise multi-location chains with AI-first platform, unicorn status at $1.5B valuation), Vagaro (predictable £20/month base with no marketplace commissions), Mindbody (multi-modality wellness combining fitness and salon services, serves 40,000+ businesses), GlossGenius (premium design-first for independent professionals, $510M valuation), Square Appointments (free tier for solopreneurs), and Goldie (mobile-first with AI marketing tools and dynamic pricing).
data.author: Dimitri Grassi
