data.full_text:
MediaNama’s Take: The new Google AI Mode inside Search signals a shift from a search engine that shows choices to an AI assistant that decides which choices matter. This change raises deeper questions about competition and market access because the AI assistant does not simply display information. It plans routes, picks hotels, filters options, and nudges users toward booking flows that Google designs. Moreover, the system sits on top of the market. It operates as the first interface that many users will now encounter, long before they reach an Online Travel Agency (OTA) or a hotel website. This is not a hypothetical concern. For context, multiple regulators and courts in India and abroad have already examined how Google shapes markets through design, billing rules, and ranking behaviour. The Testbook case in India and the Epic case in the United States show how difficult it is for smaller players to challenge platform-level design choices. Consequently, the expansion of AI Mode into travel planning could create another layer of intermediation where Google acts as a de facto gateway to discovery and bookings. The key question is simple. When an AI assistant becomes the default entry point into a sector, what safeguards are needed to ensure fairness, visibility, and meaningful competition? What’s the News Google has announced a major expansion of AI Mode inside Search, introducing new travel-planning and booking capabilities that bring itinerary creation, price discovery, and reservations into a single AI-driven flow. The company has rolled out early access to a redesigned planning interface, expanded AI-powered flight discovery, and deeper integrations with restaurant and event booking partners. These updates mark the most significant step yet in turning AI Mode into a full travel assistant rather than a search feature. Key Details of the Google AI Mode Update Canvas for Travel Planning Google has introduced Canvas, a new planning workspace that pulls real-time information on flights, hotels, routes, photos, reviews, and activities into a single side panel. Users can describe the kind of trip they want, and the assistant generates itineraries, compares hotels by price and amenities, suggests activities optimised by travel time, and refines plans through follow-up prompts. Plans can be saved and revisited through AI Mode history. Canvas is currently available on desktop in the US for users enrolled in the Labs experiment. Expanded AI-Powered Flight Deals The company has widened access to its AI-driven bargain finder within Google Flights. Travellers can describe destinations or travel styles in natural language, and the assistant identifies affordable destinations and highlights the best fares. Flight Deals now covers more than 200 countries and territories and supports over 60 languages, expanding far beyond the earlier rollout limited to the US, Canada, and India. Agentic Booking Across Services The Google AI Mode adds broader booking abilities across restaurants, events, and local services. The AI assistant can search across multiple reservation platforms, check live availability, and surface curated options. Integrated partners include OpenTable, Resy, Tock, Ticketmaster, StubHub, SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, Booksy, Fresha, and Vagaro. Restaurant reservations are rolling out widely in the US without requiring Labs opt-in, while event tickets and appointment bookings remain available to Labs users. Work-in-Progress: Flight and Hotel Bookings Inside Google AI Mode Google is developing support for completing flight and hotel bookings directly inside the AI interface. Users will be able to compare schedules, prices, room photos, amenities, and reviews conversationally before finalising bookings. To build this experience, the company is working with Booking.com, Expedia, Choice Hotels International, IHG, Marriott International, and Wyndham. A Full Travel Funnel Inside Search Together, these updates position the Google AI Mode as an end-to-end travel assistant that manages discovery, comparison, and booking inside one guided flow. Users no longer need to switch between several websites or apps to plan a trip, which is a shift that could meaningfully reshape how travel platforms, hotel chains, and OTAs reach potential customers. How Will the Google AI Mode Shape Travel Discovery Google’s AI Mode changes the way users discover options. Instead of a list of links, users will now see AI-generated suggestions. These include best times to visit, activities tailored to interests, hotel clusters, routes, price ranges, and day-by-day itineraries. The assistant also identifies top neighbourhoods, compares attractions, and suggests the most efficient ways to move between stops. This creates a guided funnel. The AI assistant reduces the user’s decision tree by selecting certain attractions, omitting others, and foregrounding hotels or destinations that fit the AI’s interpretation of the query. Moreover, the flow may end in booking prompts tied to Google Flights or partner OTAs, which means Google’s ranking, data inputs, and commercial relationships shape what the user sees first. For context, this is different from traditional search, where users receive multiple organic links and can choose freely. Here, the system structures the journey in advance. As a result, travel providers may find themselves more dependent on Google’s AI preferences, training data, and marketplace design. In comments previously shared with MediaNama, Dr Navneet Sharma, Advisor at Helicon Consulting, warned why this shift matters: “A utility-maximising recommender system may promote competitive pricing, while a revenue-maximising one can facilitate tacit collusion or favour certain suppliers.” This distinction becomes critical when the assistant becomes the dominant pathway into travel decisions. What the Testbook Stay Signals for Smaller Players The Supreme Court’s interim stay in the Testbook case highlights the procedural challenges that smaller firms may face when they attempt to challenge platform-level design decisions. Testbook, an ed-tech platform focused on competitive exam preparation, argued that Google’s billing terms were unfair, discriminatory, and drafted without negotiation. The Madras High Court allowed the suit to proceed after finding the dispute grounded in contractual issues rather than Competition Commission of India (CCI)-exclusive matters. However, Google insisted that the case belonged before regulators or arbitration channels, not civil courts. The SC stayed the suit and sent it back for review, indicating that jurisdictional questions must be resolved before any trial occurs. This pause illustrates how a smaller company can spend months debating procedure before reaching substantive questions of market power or unfair design. Therefore, if travel providers later claim that Google’s AI Mode affects their visibility or access, they may encounter similar obstacles. Additionally, the stay aligns with a broader pattern seen in other markets. When platform design choices affect smaller firms, those firms often struggle to find a clear legal pathway for timely redress. The Growing Competition Pressure of Google in India For context, Google already faces multiple competition challenges in India. The CCI identified the Play Store billing system as anti-competitive in October 2022 and penalised the company for mandatory billing, anti-steering rules, and restrictions on third-party options. The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal upheld these findings in March 2025, even though it reduced the penalty to Rs 216.69 crore from Rs 936.44 crore and altered some behavioural remedies. Additionally, Google settled a separate CCI probe involving Android TV bundling with a Rs 20.24 crore payment in April 2025. Moreover, the Commission also examined Google following complaints from WinZO about the exclusionary treatment of real-money gaming apps. In that investigation, the CCI found prima facie abuse of dominance and invited public comments on Google’s proposed remedies. These proceedings matter because they reveal a regulatory pattern. Courts and the CCI both recognise that Google’s design choices have market-level effects. At the same time, enforcement remains slow and contested, allowing the company to continue shaping markets during the years that investigations take. What the Google AI Mode Update Means for Travel Providers The Google AI Mode sits at the intersection of discovery, ranking, and booking. Therefore, the feature raises several competition questions. First, when the AI assistant chooses which hotels or attractions to highlight, it shapes visibility for providers. Smaller hotels, homestays, and OTAs may lose traffic if the assistant prioritises certain partners or generic Google-generated recommendations. In contrast, larger partners may benefit from the volume and consistency of placement. Second, the system relies heavily on data drawn from Google’s ecosystem. This creates inherent asymmetry. Google controls search history, Maps ratings, YouTube travel videos, local reviews, and flight price trends. Consequently, it can create travel pathways that no competitor can easily match. Third, this raises questions about self-preferencing. Google does not need to prefer its own service explicitly for the AI assistant to tilt outcomes. The structure of the flow itself, from information gathering to booking, can privilege the company’s signals over everyone else’s. Moreover, the CCI has repeatedly found that platform design can constitute an unfair condition under competition law. The Play Store and Android TV cases illustrate how policies that appear neutral at first glance may have structural effects. Therefore, if AI Mode becomes the default interface for travel discovery, questions about discrimination, transparency, and data use will move to the centre of policy debate. Sharma had earlier cautioned that such models “may disadvantage rival providers by relegating them to less visible positions, effectively raising rivals’ costs and excluding them over time.” His assessment applies directly to AI-led travel pathways that could privilege integrated partners and leave smaller players unseen. Why AI-Led Intermediation Raises New Questions AI Assistants as Gatekeepers AI Mode does not merely answer queries. It performs decisions on the user’s behalf. That shift has policy consequences. When users rely on the Google AI Mode instead of browsing competing websites, the assistant becomes a gatekeeper. However, India’s competition framework remains focused on past conduct rather than preventive rules for digital platforms. Therefore, even if AI-led travel planning creates market distortions, enforcement may arrive too late to matter. Additionally, the assistant’s reliance on opaque models creates transparency challenges. Providers cannot understand why their listings appear or disappear. Meanwhile, the firm can argue that ranking flows reflect model behaviour rather than discriminatory action. This ambiguity introduces a new regulatory frontier where algorithms, data, and commercial incentives interact. For context, these concerns now appear in the CCI’s Market Study on Artificial Intelligence and Competition (2025). The report warns that AI interfaces can entrench dominance faster than traditional enforcement tools can respond. It highlights risks including ecosystem lock-ins, self-preferencing, discriminatory ranking, algorithmic collusion, and “often insurmountable competitive edge” arising from control over data, compute, and user traffic. Why Current Competition Tools May Not Keep Up Sharma previously told MediaNama, in the context of AI-led travel assistants, that “India’s Competition Act primarily targets traditional collusion and abuse of dominance. AI-powered intermediaries introduce opacity, speed, and self-learning, all of which current ex-post tools may struggle to address.” That concern becomes particularly relevant when AI systems begin mediating travel discovery and bookings at scale. Notably, global regulators are already acting. The EU’s Digital Markets Act (DMA), Japan’s transparency law, and South Korea’s app store reforms recognise the risks of platform-level gatekeeping. India’s policy debate is moving in the same direction, but the framework is still catching up. For travel providers, this means the competitive landscape may soon be shaped less by price or service quality and more by how an AI assistant ranks, filters, and routes user attention. Whether India develops rules for this stage will determine who gets seen and who gets left out. Also read: How MakeMyTrip’s AI Assistant Myra Raises New Competition Concerns

With new AI-powered features in Search, you can get help building the perfect itinerary, finding a great deal on your next trip and turning your plans into bookings.

It’s holiday travel season! Whether you’re visiting family or just dreaming about next year’s big vacation, now is a great time to start planning your next trip. And thanks to our latest AI upgrades, Search can handle some of the heavy lifting: New AI-powered features can help you build the perfect itinerary, find the best deals and turn your plans into bookings. Build your travel plans with Canvas in AI Mode Canvas is a tool in AI Mode that gives you a space to organize plans and projects over time. And now, you can use Canvas to build travel plans that are customized for your specific needs. Just tell AI Mode what type of trip you’re planning and the recommendations you’re looking for, then select the option to “Create Canvas.” Right away, you’ll get a plan in the Canvas side panel that brings together real-time Search data for flights and hotels, details from Google Maps like photos and reviews and relevant information from sites across the web. You’ll find suggestions that fit your criteria, like hotel comparisons based on pricing and amenities or ideas for restaurants and activities optimized by travel time from where you’re staying. To refine the plan and make it your own, you can ask follow-up questions and get help with tradeoffs, like choosing a hotel that’s closer to brunch but a bit further from hiking trails. If you want to take a break, you can always jump back in and come back to the plan through your AI Mode history, via the menu on the top-left. Travel planning with Canvas is available on desktop in the U.S. for those opted into the AI Mode experiment in Labs. Find airfare bargains with AI-powered Flight Deals Today, we’re announcing the global expansion of Flight Deals, an AI-powered search tool we’re testing within Google Flights that recently launched in the U.S., Canada and India. It’s designed for flexible travelers who want to quickly find affordable destinations and save money on their next trip. To get started, just describe where, when and how you’d like to travel — like you’re talking to a friend — and Flight Deals will use AI to understand what you’re looking for and show the best bargains available. Flight Deals has started rolling out to more than 200 countries and territories worldwide, including the U.K., France, Germany, Mexico, Brazil, Indonesia, Japan and Korea, along with support for more than 60 languages. Turn plans into bookings with agentic AI This week, we’re bringing AI Mode’s agentic capabilities to even more people, so you can take the hassle out of booking things, like restaurant reservations, event tickets or beauty and wellness appointments. Just describe what you’re looking for with all your needs and preferences and AI Mode will search across multiple reservation platforms and websites to find real-time availability for options that meet your criteria. Then, AI Mode will show you a curated list to choose from, with direct links so you can finalize your booking through partners like OpenTable, Resy, Tock, Ticketmaster, StubHub, SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, Booksy, Fresha and Vagaro. Agentic booking for restaurants is rolling out this week on AI Mode in the U.S. (no Labs opt-in required), so you can easily make plans for family dinners, date nights, holiday brunches and more. And as we recently shared, agentic booking for event tickets and local appointments is available to all U.S. Labs users. In the future, we’ll also make it possible to finish booking flights and hotels directly in AI Mode. We’re working with industry partners to build an experience where you can simply describe what you’re looking for to compare different flights or hotels and browse helpful information like schedules, prices, room photos, amenities and reviews. You’ll be able to follow up and refine your options, and then once you’re ready, you can quickly complete the booking with the partner of your choice. Building a helpful experience for travelers requires deep collaboration with the industry, and we’re already working with partners including Booking.com, Choice Hotels International, Expedia, IHG Hotels & Resorts, Marriott International and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts to make this possible. We’re committed to partnering with travel companies of every size so you have all the best options at your fingertips. With today’s updates, AI will handle more of the busywork — so you can spend less time planning and more time having fun.

data.title: 14 Best Club Management Software Tools That Save Time and Money
data.ai_summary: The article reviews various club management software options that help streamline administrative tasks, enhance member engagement, and support club growth, applicable to different types of clubs including social, private, sports, and wellness clubs. data.author: Marlena Moore
data.full_text:
Managing a club is more than just fun and games; from tracking members and dues to event registrations and newsletters, it can become overwhelming – especially if you’re just using spreadsheets.

If you find yourself spread thin, wearing many hats and trying to deliver the best possible experience for your members, club management software might be for you.

Whether your club has 50 members or 5,000, it can transform the way you run your organization, allowing you to create memorable experiences, grow your membership and make every moment with your club count.

Modern club management platforms are incredibly versatile. From sports and hobby clubs to private or social organizations, you can customize tech to fit your organization’s unique needs.

In this post, we’ll go over:

What does club management software do

The benefits – for both you and your members

Features to look for when choosing a club management solution

How to choose the best club management system for your needs

14 of the most popular software options, plus which type of club they’re best suited for

Ready to modernize your club and provide a better experience for your members?

Let’s dive in!

What Is Club Management Software?

Club management software is an all-in-one solution that helps clubs grow their membership while saving time and money. It does this by automating administrative tasks for running a member-based organization and by offering tools and features that elevate the member experience. Think about all the emails you send – newsletters, event promotions, fundraising, volunteer opportunities – club management software can automate it for your club. Run a lot of events? Building registration forms, tracking attendees and sending out post-event surveys becomes simplified.

Whether you’re managing a private social club with exclusive memberships or a community-based hobby club, modern platforms help you save hours each week. Essentially, this is tech that allows you to organize, communicate and deliver more value to your members — all while cutting back on admin work. We’ll deep dive into the features to look for in club management solutions in the following sections.

Why Should I Use Club Management Software?

No matter what kind of club you run, club management software is there to make your job easier while boosting member engagement. Here are just a few of the benefits it can offer:

Faster Membership Growth

For many clubs, attracting new members is the greatest challenge. Thankfully, club management tools can help! Many offer a website builder and basic marketing features like email and text messaging tools, to help you spread the word about your organization and attract new members.

Read more: 99 Ways To Get New Members For Your Organization

Increase Member Retention Rates

Club management tools are designed to help you engage with your members and give them the best experience possible by putting everything your members need in one place. With a professional website, members can learn about upcoming events, when you’re open to the public and much more, all from your homepage.

Many solutions also offer a members-only login that lets them access your gated resources, connect with other members, and easily update their profiles.

A great experience with your club brings members back to use your services or join your events, again and again!

Read more: Your Complete Guide To Increase Member Engagement

For example, the Ski Bees Club’s website is full of great information about their organization. With a user-friendly design and eye-catching imagery, prospective and returning members can learn about what’s happening next, the benefits they offer and see members in action.

Saves Time — Lots of It

Club management tools can automate almost all of your administrative tasks, which means you can stop spending hours filing paperwork and chasing down payments and focus on what really matters: building relationships with your members.

“Because our club is short-staffed, WildApricot has been a lifesaver! It saves me over 20 hours a week and their support has been fantastic.” – Gary Rubens, Ski Club of Washington D.C.

Read more The Complete Guide to Marketing Automation for Nonprofits + Top Tools to Use

Powerful Analytics

Wondering what type of events get the most attendance? Or what types of emails your members are most likely to respond to?

With comprehensive reporting tools, you can get valuable insights into your membership. Club management software can analyze which of your tactics are working best from email stats, event/meeting attendance, survey responses and more. This allows you to keep doing the activities your club’s members like best, without wasting time on the rest — it’s a win-win!

Read more: Why Your Organization Needs a Member Satisfaction Survey and 40+ Question Examples

8 Must-Have Features To Look For in Club Management Software

The best club management software solutions include functionalities like:

Event management : registration forms, attendance tracking and promotional tools

Payment processing : securely take dues, renewals, donations, ticketing and more

Club website : easy-to-update with embeds like event calendar, social media and resource library

Communication tools : automate emails, text messages, newsletters and invoices

Contact database: Search, filter and update members, donors and subscribers

Financial tools : create and analyze reports on dues, donations, sales and event tickets

Mobile app : manage and communicate with members on the go

Below, we’ve also outlined which type of club these features matter most for.

Club Software Feature Summary Table

Feature Description Best For Online Registration & Payments Streamline event and membership signups, as well as dues collection All clubs

Website Builder Keep members informed and attract new ones Social & private clubs Automated Communications Send newsletters, invoices and reminders All clubs Analytics & Reports Track performance and trends Growing clubs Scheduling & Bookings Manage classes, event, or facilities Private and activity-based clubs Access Control Secure member-only access Private or gated clubs Mobile App Manage and connect on the go All clubs

📘 Still using Excel to manage your club? Here’s why it’s the perfect time to move past your club membership Excel template.

How to Pick the Right Club Management Platform For Your Club

Choosing the right club management software depends on your club’s size, type and goals – but it’s also about where your club is headed.

In today’s digital era, we’ve seen a massive transformation in how clubs operate. Embracing technology is more critical than ever for membership-based organizations to achieve major growth and success.

For example, many private and social clubs blend in-person and virtual experiences through hybrid memberships, digital access passes and automated scheduling tools. What once required manual coordination can now be managed from one dashboard.

These features help clubs deliver the seamless, member-first experience today’s audiences expect. What’s not to love?

As you evaluate platforms, ask yourself these questions to focus on the core features and considerations that will keep your club efficient, connected and ready for the next wave of digital growth.

1. What Type of Club Are You?

Private clubs often need access control, tiered memberships and exclusive communication tools that maintain a sense of prestige and privacy.

Social clubs might prioritize event management, community engagement and modern communication channels to keep members connected.

Hobby or volunteer clubs may prefer simple, affordable and easy-to-learn systems that reduce admin work for part-time organizers.

Read more: 501c7 vs 501c3: Club or Cause—What’s Your Type?

2. What’s My Budget?

Club management software can cost as low as $63/month for 100 contacts, but prices can increase from there depending on the features and functionality you need, as well as how many members you have.

Start with what fits your club today, but consider choosing software that can grow as your community expands. Plus, look for platforms that support integrations, so you’re not locked into a limited system as your needs grow. Be sure to look for any hidden setup fees, so you’re not surprised by a larger bill than expected.

3. How Easy Is It To Use?

Your software should be intuitive for everyone to use, whether they’re a club manager, a volunteer or a longtime member. A clean, easy interface reduces training time and boosts adoption. As Gaylen from East York Probus Club says,

“It really comes down to protecting your volunteers. It’s hard to get volunteers these days. Everybody’s got stuff going on. They want to participate, but they don’t want to get stuck doing grunt work.”

Read the full case study here.

This is particularly important if your club is volunteer-run or you only have a couple of paid staff members — you don’t want to have to spend too much time learning a complicated platform. Your club management software should also offer guides or help articles to help you learn how to use it on your own, so you can get up and running without relying on external support.

4. What Does It Integrate With?

Though software for club management is often a one-stop shop, you may have certain specific needs that it doesn’t cover — or perhaps you already have tools you love and don’t want to leave.

If your club uses multiple web, financial and email marketing tools, check if the software solution you’re evaluating has native integrations. The more your systems “talk” to each other, the less manual work you’ll have to do.

For example, WildApricot offers built-in integrations with QuickBooks, WordPress and popular payment gateways, so private and social clubs can automatically sync financial data, manage website updates and send targeted email campaigns without switching between multiple platforms. That kind of seamless connectivity saves hours every month and keeps your club’s operations running smoothly.

5. How Secure is It?

Strong data protection is non-negotiable in 2025. With rising privacy standards and greater use of online payments, choose a vendor that takes compliance and encryption seriously. Look for tools that comply with regulations such as PCI, GDPR and CCPA.

Now that you have these questions in mind, it’s time to start evaluating your options! The best club software for your organization will be the one that fits your exact needs. Below are 14 of the most popular, proven options for 2025 and beyond.

Mobile app for members and admins to manage your club on the go

Posted on October 31, 2025 by staff Booksy Biz UK: Insights from real users Share:

Partner content If you run a salon, barbershop or any service business in the UK you know the grind is real. A good booking system is not nice to have, it’s a lifesaver. You’ve probably heard of Booksy Biz as it’s a big name in the business management app world. It promises to be an all in one solution to book appointments, manage clients and market your services. But does it deliver? We dived into hundreds of reviews from UK business owners to get the lowdown. We’ll look at what people love, what drives them mad and whether Booksy Biz is the right partner for your business. So, What Exactly is Booksy Biz? Think of Booksy Biz as your digital front desk, personal assistant, and marketing guru all rolled into one app. It is a complete management tool built for service pros like hairstylists, barbers, and nail techs. The whole idea is to simplify your day-to-day operations so you can focus on your clients. Here is a quick rundown of what it does: Calendar Management : You get a customizable calendar where you can color-code services and easily manage or reschedule appointments.

Client Management: The app stores all your client info, their appointment history, and their preferences, which makes it easy to build great relationships.

Mobile Payments: Booksy offers secure payment processing, so you can take payments online or in person with tap-to-pay and a card reader. You can also set up cancellation policies and require deposits to protect your income.

Marketing Tools: It comes packed with email and SMS marketing tools, a social post creator, and automated campaigns to help you get the word out. Booksy and Its Competitors Let’s tackle the big question: booksy vs fresha? You will see this debate pop up everywhere when you look for booking software. While the sources do not give us a head-to-head feature battle, it is clear that business owners often consider Fresha as a top alternative. Your final choice will likely come down to what your specific business needs. People also frequently compare Booksy to other platforms like StyleSeat, Square Appointments, and Vagaro before they make a decision. So, What’s the Good News? What Users Love Many business owners are huge fans of Booksy Biz, and for good reason. They praise its simple interface, smart scheduling, and powerful marketing tools that genuinely help them grow. Effortless Scheduling and Management The number one thing people rave about? It just makes scheduling so much easier. Clients can book themselves anytime, day or night, even at 3 am. This frees you from the constant back-and-forth of phone calls and messages, which lets you focus on the client in your chair. Plus, those automated reminders are a game-changer for cutting down on no-shows. A Powerful Tool for Client Growth Booksy is not just a calendar; it is a client-magnet for many users. The app’s marketing tools, especially the social media integration, help businesses get seen. The “Boost” feature, although it has a cost, gets a lot of credit for bringing in new customers. One barber even said he gets two to three new clients every week just from being on the app. For new stylists, it is a fantastic way to build a client list from scratch. Streamlined Business Operations Beyond booking, Booksy helps you run your whole operation from one place. Users love the built-in payment system for taking prepayments and deposits, which secures their income. The platform also offers great analytics and financial reports that give you a clear picture of how your business performs. Okay, But What are The Downsides It is not all perfect. Some users share stories of serious frustration with terrible customer support, unexpected costs, and annoying technical glitches. These issues have been big enough to make some loyal customers look for another option. Customer Support Woes The biggest red flag, mentioned over and over, is the customer support. Users describe the support team as unhelpful, slow, or just plain unreachable. People report endless wait times on the phone, emails that take weeks to get a reply, and chat support that leaves them hanging for hours. This has left business owners feeling ignored, belittled, and stuck with major problems. Costs and Hidden Fees Let’s talk money. For some, the monthly subscription of £40.00 is a bit steep compared to other options. On top of that, users complain about what they feel are “hidden charges”. These include transaction fees for payment processing and the commission for the Boost feature. data.full_text: Source: Liberis Liberis, a leading global embedded finance provider, has announced the US launch of its new Buy Now, Pay Later product, Pay with Liberis. Vagaro, a leading business management platform for the beauty, wellness, and fitness industries, is the first of Liberis’ strategic partners to adopt the new product, which will be offered to their customers as capital for hardware. Vagaro’s users can now purchase products or services at checkout and pay through a fixed percentage of future revenue, solving one of SMBs’ most persistent challenges. This launch establishes Liberis at the forefront of embedded finance innovation, with Liberis and Vagaro collaborating closely on the creation of Pay with Liberis to ensure it was suitable to solve the financing pain points of Vagaro’s users. “Small businesses must navigate a fragmented financing landscape, and businesses within the beauty, health and wellness industries face specific funding issues that require specialised support,” said Rob Fairfield, chief executive officer of Liberis. “With Pay with Liberis, we are now able to offer seamless embedded finance offerings that are not only hand-crafted solutions, but actually accelerate growth, as we lead the way in building definitive funding ecosystems.” Bespoke offerings for beauty, health and wellness SMBs Within Vagaro’s platform, Pay with Liberis will be offered to customers as capital for hardware, and will offer financing for SMBs from $500 and up to $10,000, although Vagaro’s initial rollout will be capped at $3,000. Pay with Liberis is integrated seamlessly into Vagaro’s checkout process, with merchants able to finance hardware and similar purchases at checkout with funds disbursed directly to Vagaro. Customers can benefit immensely from this integration, with payments automatically split from daily revenue, and no early payment penalties. This product also serves as a gateway to Vagaro’s other financial offerings powered by Liberis, such as Vagaro Capital. Pay with Liberis expands SMB access to growth enabling tools, such as marketing spend and POS hardware, all whilst customers can track repayments and download statements via their dashboard. “When accessing financial services, we want to help our merchants achieve success and remove some of the obstacles they face,” said Kerry Melchior, chief operating officer at Vagaro. “Collaborating closely with Liberis on capital for hardware, we have been able to prioritise our customers’ needs and reinforce our commitment to supporting our merchant community.” Pay with Liberis is now live in the US with plans for expansion into other markets over the course of 2026. data.full_text: Liberis has launched its first Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) financing product in the US through a partnership with business management platform Vagaro. The initiative aims to expand small business access to financing options directly within the checkout experience. Through this collaboration, Vagaro will integrate Pay with Liberis as Capital for Hardware, allowing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to finance purchases such as hardware or point-of-sale equipment. Funding will range from USD 500 up to USD 10,000, though the initial rollout is limited to USD 3,000. Payments will be automatically deducted as a set percentage of future revenue, with no penalties for early repayment. Funds are disbursed directly to Vagaro, ensuring a streamlined transaction process for merchants. Addressing financing barriers in niche service sectors The embedded financing tool was developed jointly by Liberis and Vagaro to address specific funding challenges faced by small companies in the beauty, wellness, and fitness sectors. Representatives from Liberis noted that businesses in these industries often struggle with fragmented access to financing and require solutions tailored to their revenue cycles. By embedding the BNPL function within Vagaro’s platform, merchants can manage repayments and access financial information directly through their dashboard. The new offering also connects to Vagaro’s other funding solutions powered by Liberis, including Vagaro Capital. Vagaro officials said the collaboration with Liberis was designed to simplify financing for merchants and reduce barriers to obtaining growth-related funding. The company highlighted that the joint product represents an effort to prioritise merchant needs and improve access to capital. Pay with Liberis is currently available to Vagaro customers in the US, with expansion into additional markets planned for 2026.

ATLANTA & LONDON, October 27, 2025--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Liberis, a leading global embedded finance provider, has today announced the U.S. launch of its new Buy Now, Pay Later product, Pay with Liberis. Vagaro, a leading business management platform for the beauty, wellness, and fitness industries, is the first of Liberis’ strategic partners to adopt the new product – which will be offered to their customers as Capital for Hardware. Vagaro’s users can now purchase products or services at checkout and pay through a fixed percentage of future revenue, solving one of SMBs most persistent challenges. This launch establishes Liberis at the forefront of embedded finance innovation, with Liberis and Vagaro collaborating closely on the creation of Pay with Liberis to ensure it was suitable to solve the financing pain points of Vagaro’s users. "Small businesses must navigate a fragmented financing landscape, and businesses within the beauty, health and wellness industries face specific funding issues that require specialised support" says Rob Fairfield, CEO of Liberis. "With Pay with Liberis, we are now able to offer seamless embedded finance offerings that are not only hand-crafted solutions, but actually accelerate growth, as we lead the way in building definitive funding ecosystems." Bespoke offerings for beauty, health and wellness SMBs: Within Vagaro’s platform, Pay with Liberis will be offered to customers as Capital for Hardware, and will offer financing for SMBs from $500 and up to $10,000, although Vagaro’s initial rollout will be capped at $3,000. Pay with Liberis is integrated seamlessly into Vagaro’s checkout process, with merchants able to finance hardware and similar purchases at checkout with funds disbursed directly to Vagaro. Customers can benefit immensely from this integration, with payments automatically split from daily revenue, and no early payment penalties. This product also serves as a gateway to Vagaro’s other financial offerings powered by Liberis, such as Vagaro Capital. Pay with Liberis expands SMB access to growth enabling tools, such as marketing spend and POS hardware, all whilst customers can track repayments and download statements via their dashboard. "When accessing financial services, we want to help our merchants achieve success and remove some of the obstacles they face," says Kerry Melchior, COO of Vagaro. "Collaborating closely with Liberis on Capital for Hardware, we have been able to prioritise our customers’ needs and reinforce our commitment to supporting our merchant community."

Pay with Liberis is now live in the U.S. with plans for expansion into other markets over the course of 2026. At its core, Liberis is a technology-driven company, bridging the gap between finance and small businesses. They use data and insights to help partners understand their customers' real time needs and tech to offer tailor-made financial products. Empowering small businesses to grow and keep their independent spirit alive is central to their vision. Since 2007, Liberis has funded over 50,000 small businesses with over $3bn - but they believe there is much more to be done. Vagaro's a-la-carte options and affordable pricing provide a unique level of scalability, making it suitable for businesses of all sizes, from the solopreneur to enterprise franchises.
